AboutResponse.description: What this server is built from, and where else it can be reached.

bolt.description: The Bolt server, when it is on and listening; absent otherwise

components.description: The server first, then the libraries it is built on

sql.description: The SQL door, when it is on and listening; absent otherwise

AccountRefusal.description: A refusal from the account surface. Carries only the reason; the status code is the only other fact and the body does not repeat it

error.description: Why the request was refused, written to be shown

ActionCommandConfig.description: A slash command that runs a world action when a chat message starts with it. Listed by GET /commands and saved by POST /commands

actionName.description: Name of the world action the command runs. Text typed after the command word becomes the action's input; with none, the action runs directly if it takes no input and otherwise asks for it with a form

command.description: The command word without its leading slash, matched case-insensitively. Also the file name it is saved under, so saving one that exists replaces it

description.description: The message shown with that input form. Empty when not set

ActionListItem.description: One action the agent platform can plan with, as GET /actions lists it and as each agent from GET /agent-platform/agents nests it.

canRerun.description: True when the action may run again in an agent process where it has already run

deletable.description: True only when the action's YAML lives directly in this world's config/actions directory, so DELETE /actions/spec/{name} can remove it; false for realm-shipped and platform-defined actions

description.description: What the action does, as its definition states it

inputTypes.description: Names of the types the action needs as input

name.description: Identifier the agent platform knows the action by; for a world action, the name /actions/spec/{name} takes

outputTypes.description: Names of the types the action produces

readOnly.description: True when the action declares that it has no external side effects

ActionRefusal.description: A refused action operation: not found, not editable, not deletable, or a compilation that failed

message.description: Why, written to be shown, naming the action

ActionSpecDetail.description: One action's spec. The prompt, types, tools, references and model are present only for a prompted action, and absent, not null, for any other

description.description: What the action does

editable.description: True only for a prompted action defined directly in this world, which is the only kind editable here

inputTypeNames.description: The types the action takes. Prompted actions only

llmModel.description: The model the action runs on. Prompted actions only, and null there for the default

llmTemperature.description: The sampling temperature. Prompted actions only, and null there for the default

name.description: The action's name

outputTypeName.description: The type the action produces. Prompted actions only, and null there when none is set

prompt.description: The prompt template. Prompted actions only

references.description: The references the action reads. Prompted actions only

stepType.description: The kind of step the spec defines

tools.description: The tools the action may call. Prompted actions only

ActivityJobStats.description: One job's run durations, in milliseconds

failures.description: How many of the counted runs failed

label.description: The job's label, the same sentence the activity list shows for its runs

lastEndedAt.description: When the job's latest counted run ended, an ISO-8601 UTC instant

mine.description: True when the job runs for the caller; false for the appliance's own, which carries no user

ActivityRow.description: One piece of work the appliance is doing or has just finished, or a pinned failure, as GET /activity lists it. Held in memory only

detail.description: Why it ended the way it did, such as the failure message. Null while it runs

endedAt.description: When the work ended, an ISO-8601 UTC instant; on a pinned row, its latest failure. Null while it runs

failures.description: How many times a pinned job has failed since it began failing. Null on an ordinary row

id.description: The activity's id; for a pinned failure, "pin:" followed by its label

label.description: What the work is, as a sentence about its subject, such as "Learning the X API". Identifies a job across runs, and is what a pin is dismissed by

mine.description: True when the work is being done for the caller; false for the appliance's own work, which carries no user. Other users' work is never listed

pinned.description: True for a job that failed and has not worked since. The row stays until the job next succeeds or the pin is dismissed

startedAt.description: When the work began, an ISO-8601 UTC instant. On a pinned row, when the job began failing

state.description: Whether it is still running or how it ended. Always FAILED on a pinned row

type.description: A stable machine name for the kind of work, where a client may need to tell kinds apart, such as document.ingest, document.figures or document.mentions. Null for most work, and on pinned rows

ActivityStats.description: How long each job takes over its most recent runs since the app started, answered by GET /activity/stats

jobs.description: One entry per job, slowest 95th percentile first

runsPerJob.description: How many of each job's most recent runs the figures cover, at most

since.description: When the oldest run counted here began, an ISO-8601 UTC instant. Null when nothing has settled since the app started

AddApiRequest.description: An API to save to the world

auth.description: Auth scheme the API expects, e.g. bearer

token_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the token

url.description: The spec URL — an OpenAPI document or a GraphQL endpoint

AddRealmRequest.description: Where to install a realm from, the body of POST /realms: a git repository to clone, or a realm directory already mounted into the appliance

confirmed.description: Set true only once the user has confirmed installing an experimental realm, after a 409 with status needs-confirmation. Ignored for a path install

path.description: Absolute path, inside the appliance container, of a mounted realm directory with a realm.yml, such as /realms/realm-esg. Loaded in place, never cloned or copied; the directory's name becomes the realm's. Takes precedence over repo

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit SHA to check out. Null for the repository's default branch. Ignored for a path install

repo.description: The repository to clone: owner/repo for GitHub, or a full clone URL. Required unless path is given, and ignored when it is

AgentListItem.description: One agent the platform hosts, with its own actions and goals, as GET /agent-platform/agents lists it.

actions.description: The agent's own actions, sorted by name

description.description: What the agent does, as its definition states it

goals.description: The agent's own goals, sorted by name

name.description: Identifier the agent platform knows the agent by

provider.description: Who provides the agent, as its definition declares

AgentProposal.description: A better version of an agent, proposed by the agent from its own record, with the evidence for each change. Made by POST /agents/{name}/reflect, listed by GET /agents/{name}/proposals, settled by its adopt and dismiss endpoints

agent.description: Name of the agent the proposal is for

changes.description: The proposed changes, already filtered to the targets a proposal may touch; may be empty when the record supported nothing

createdAt.description: When the proposal was made, ISO-8601 instant

decidedAt.description: When it was adopted or dismissed, ISO-8601 instant; null while OPEN

fromVersion.description: The agent's latest signed version when the proposal was made, which it improves on; null when the agent had never been signed

id.description: Proposal id, "pr_" followed by a UUID; the {id} of the adopt and dismiss endpoints

ownerId.description: Id of the user whose world the agent belongs to; proposals are private to them

proven.description: Whether the proposal has passed a battery and a replay of the period; always false, since neither check exists yet

record.description: The record the reflection read, as plain-text lines of counts over the period: runs by outcome, requests by status, hours to a decision, the commonest rejection reasons, and each duty's cadence

refused.description: Why the last attempt to adopt it was refused, because the result would widen what the agent may do; null when no adoption has been refused

status.description: OPEN until adopted or dismissed; a refused adoption leaves it OPEN

summary.description: The model's one-sentence summary of what the proposal changes

AgentReflectionProposalResponse.description: A proposal after reflecting, adopting or dismissing, or why that was refused; answered by the /agents/{name}/reflect and /agents/{name}/proposals/{id} endpoints

proposal.description: The proposal after the change; null when it was refused

refused.description: Why the change was refused, in words; null when it was made

AgentRequest.description: A gateway call held for a person to approve or reject: the verb a routine wants called, or a person's own held call, with its arguments, why, and the evidence. Listed by GET /requests, fetched by GET /requests/{id}, returned by POST /requests/{id}/decision.

about.description: Whom or what the call is about, by name (e.g. the customer a note goes on); null when the call did not say

agent.description: Agent whose run raised it, shown to the approver as who is asking; null when no agent holds the routine or a person asked

args.description: The verb's input, as a JSON-encoded string

decidedAt.description: When it was approved or rejected, or for an expired one its expiresAt, as an ISO-8601 instant; null while pending

decidedBy.description: Username of the person who approved or rejected it; null while pending and for an expired request

detail.description: What would happen and why, in the business's words; what the approver reads first

evidence.description: Rows the routine read that made it ask, as it saw them when it asked; at most 50, empty when it gave none

expiresAt.description: When an unanswered request expires, as an ISO-8601 instant; three days after raisedAt

id.description: Identifier of the request, `req_` followed by a UUID; the {id} in /requests/{id}

ownerId.description: User id of the person in whose world the request was raised, and who decides it

quote.description: Text the call would write where people read it (a note, a message), as it would land; null when the call writes none or did not say

raisedAt.description: When it was raised, as an ISO-8601 instant

raisedBy.description: User id of the person whose own call, made outside any routine run, was held for approval; null when a routine or an agent asked

raisedByName.description: Display name of raisedBy at the time they asked; null when raisedBy is null

reason.description: Why it was rejected, as the rejecter wrote it; null unless status is REJECTED

result.description: What the verb answered once approved, or its error when status is FAILED, truncated to 2000 characters; null until approved

routine.description: Name of the routine that raised it; `(unnamed routine)` when no routine did, as for a person's own held call

runId.description: Id of the routine run it was raised in; null when it was raised outside any run

secondPersonAsked.description: True when the verb's publisher asks for an approver other than the caller. Advisory: the world does not enforce it

selfApproved.description: True when it was approved by the same person who raised it (raisedBy); allowed, and recorded so

status.description: PENDING until decided; then APPROVED (the verb succeeded), FAILED (approved, but the verb answered an error), REJECTED, or EXPIRED (nobody answered before expiresAt)

untrusted.description: Text from outside the business the routine read before asking, each as `source: what`, sorted; the draft came after it. Empty when it read none

verb.description: Gateway tool to call on approval, e.g. `odoo_partnerMessagePost`

AgentRun.description: One run of an agent's work as the run ledger keeps it: a routine, a repair, a duty check, a conversation or a test, from start to end. Listed by GET /agents/{name}/runs and returned by GET /agents/{name}/runs/{id}

agent.description: Name of the agent holding the work; null for a routine no agent holds

agentDigest.description: SHA-256 hex digest of that signed version; null with agentVersion

agentVersion.description: The signed version number the run went as; null when no signed version governs the agent, or no agent holds the work

chain.description: For a run that answers a colleague, the names of the agents that asked, in order; empty otherwise

endedAt.description: ISO-8601 instant the run ended; null while it is running

error.description: Why it failed or timed out, up to 1,000 characters; for a duty check, why its state is unknown. Null otherwise

id.description: The run's id, `run_` and a UUID: the {id} in GET /agents/{name}/runs/{id}

kind.description: `ROUTINE`, `REPAIR` (a duty's repair run on one violation), `DUTY_CHECK`, `CONVERSATION` or `TEST`

notes.description: For a duty check, source warnings that left its rows sound, such as a cost note from a realm's producer

observing.description: True when the run only observed: its writes were refused and recorded as calls it would have made

outcome.description: `RUNNING`, `DONE`, `FAILED`, `TIMED_OUT` (including a run the appliance lost track of, closed once 30 minutes old), or `SKIPPED` (a scheduled firing that did not run; output says why). A duty check that could not read the world is `FAILED`

output.description: The last 4,000 characters it printed, the partial result when it timed out; for a skipped firing, why it did not run

ownerId.description: Id of the user whose world the run belongs to

principal.description: The agent as a principal, `agent:<name>@<world>`, apart from the account in runAs; null for duty checks, skipped firings and work no agent holds

repairs.description: For a duty check, how many violations it set out to repair; null for other runs

requests.description: Ids of the approval requests it raised

runAs.description: Username of the account the run acted as

spendByModel.description: What its model calls cost, in US cents, keyed by model name

spendCents.description: What its model calls cost in total, in US cents; 0 until the run ends

violations.description: For a duty check, the violations it found; null for other runs and for a check that could not read the world

work.description: What ran: the routine's name, the duty's name for a duty check, or `conversation:<agent>` for a conversation

AgentSpec.description: An agent as authored in its YAML file (config/agents/<name>.yml in a world, agents/<name>.yml in a realm): a named colleague with a job, a sponsor, and the routines, duties and sweeps it holds. Carried as the draft definition on an agent suggestion. Unknown fields are ignored

authority.description: What it may do on its own, verb by verb, once on duty. Null leaves every verb at act

budget.description: Its hard limits on spend and activity; raising one waits for its sponsor's signature. Null is no limit

colleagues.description: Which colleagues it may message and which may message it; both sides must agree. Null is nobody, either way

conversation.description: How it is talked to: the realms a conversation reaches and the host tools it keeps. Null scopes it to the realm that shipped it, with every host tool

disclosesAsAgent.description: Whether its writes say an agent made them, even under its own account. True by default

identity.description: Whose account each API is called with, keyed by API name: own-account (its own credential) or on-behalf-of (its sponsor's, the default)

job.description: The job in one sentence: what a manager reads first. An agent with no job cannot go on duty

models.description: Model names keyed by LLM role (for example vc_relevance), used for its own views, routines and conversations ahead of the world's role map and the deployment default

name.description: The agent's name, unique in the world; an agent with no name is not loaded

operators.description: Usernames of its operators. Dropped from a realm-shipped agent

owners.description: Usernames of its owners, who may sign it, put it back on duty after a sponsor stands it down, and move a Gatekeeper rule from observe to enforce. Dropped from a realm-shipped agent

persona.description: Slug of a personality to speak through; null for none

qos.description: How its work is scheduled, and the models it falls back to when one fails. Null is business priority with no fallbacks

realm.description: Set by the loader: the realm that shipped this agent, or null for one authored in the world

routines.description: The TypeScript actions it holds, by name; each body stays in its own action file

routing.description: "Ask me about...": when people and other agents should come to it

sponsor.description: Username of the person who answers for it. Required to go on duty; dropped from a realm-shipped agent, which the world adopts

stage.description: Its stage: off (the default), observing or on; a bare YAML boolean reads as on or off, and an unrecognised value as off. Forced to off for a realm-shipped agent

state.description: Lifecycle state: draft (the default), submitted, active, suspended or retired; an unrecognised value reads as draft. A realm-shipped agent arrives active unless it is retired

sweeps.description: The cold materializations it keeps filled, each a saved view run under its budget until a pass buys nothing. Empty sweeps nothing

version.description: A version number as written in the file; the catalogue shows the latest signed version instead

AgentSuggestion.description: A suggested colleague: work nobody has automated, its evidence, and either an installed realm agent to adopt or an agent definition to draft. Listed by GET /agent-suggestions and taken by POST /agent-suggestions, where the server sets id, ownerId, status, createdAt, decidedAt and preview

adopt.description: Name of the installed realm agent that already covers this work; null when an agent is to be drafted instead

agent.description: The agent definition to draft, in the agents YAML shape; null when adopting. The server strips sponsor, owners and operators and bounds its authority, so a draft starts unsigned and off duty

createdAt.description: When the suggestion was last recorded, as an ISO-8601 instant; set by the server

decidedAt.description: When it was drafted, adopted or dismissed, as an ISO-8601 instant; null while OPEN

evidence.description: The counts the suggestion rests on, each with the query that produced it; at least one is required

feasibility.description: Free text on whether the work can be done with what is installed: the verbs that exist, or what must be built or learned first

id.description: Server-assigned identifier, prefixed sg_; kept when an open suggestion of the same name is replaced. Ignored on POST

job.description: The work the colleague would take on, in one sentence; required

kind.description: WORKS for an agent with duties and routines, TALKS for one people converse with (a persona and realms, no duties)

name.description: The colleague's name: the realm agent to adopt, or the name the draft is written under. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, 2-40 characters

ownerId.description: Id of the user whose world the suggestion is for; set by the server to the caller

preview.description: One line per duty saying how many rows its view would act on today, or why it could not run; empty until drafted

rank.description: The scout's ranking, weighing value and feasibility together; lists are ordered by it, highest first

status.description: OPEN until a person decides; then DRAFTED, ADOPTED or DISMISSED. Always OPEN when recorded

uncovered.description: What the agent named by adopt does not cover, in a sentence; null when it covers all of the work

AgentSuggestionEvidence.description: One counted piece of evidence for an agent suggestion: what was seen, how often, over what period, and the query that counted it so it can be run again

count.description: How many times it was seen over the period

period.description: The span the count covers, as free text, e.g. "2026-04-06 to 2026-06-22"; empty when not stated

query.description: The Cypher query that produced the count, so a person can run it again; null when not given

sample.description: Example rows the query returned, each a map of column name to value; empty when none were kept

summary.description: What was seen, in a sentence, e.g. the habit or the manual act counted

AgentVersionView.description: One signed version of an agent, without the routine bodies it carries; listed newest first by GET /agents/{name}/versions

digest.description: Hex SHA-256 of what was signed: the agent's definition, its routines, the views its duties name and its persona

routines.description: Names of the routines this version holds, including any duty's repair routine

signedAt.description: When it was signed, ISO-8601 instant

signedBy.description: Username of the user who signed it

version.description: Version number, counting up from 1 with each signature

AgentView.description: An agent as GET /agents and GET /agents/{name} show it: its declaration resolved against the routines, signatures and stages this world holds. Existing routines no declared agent names appear gathered into one agent per realm, or one for the user

authority.description: What it may do on its own, verb by verb, as declared and as the Gatekeeper enforces it; null when it declares none, which leaves every verb at act

budget.description: The hard limits it runs within, as declared; null when it declares none

duties.description: The duties it keeps, each with what its latest check found

identity.description: Whose account it calls each API with, keyed by API name: own-account or on-behalf-of. An API not named is called on its sponsor's behalf

job.description: The job in one sentence, as declared; for a gathered agent, a sentence saying where its routines came from

name.description: The agent's name, unique in this world. A gathered agent is named after its realm, or `personal` for your own routines; one that collides with a declared agent takes a `-routines` suffix

needs.description: What must be fixed before it can go on duty, one phrase each ("a sponsor", "a job", a missing routine or sweep view, a signature, ...). Empty when nothing stands in the way

operators.description: Usernames of its operators, as declared; empty for a realm-shipped or gathered agent

origin.description: Where it was declared: "world", the name of the realm that ships it, or "migrated" for an agent gathered from existing routines

owners.description: Usernames of its owners: they may sign it, put it back on duty after a sponsor stands it down, and move a Gatekeeper rule from observe to enforce. Empty for a realm-shipped agent until the world declares some

persona.description: Slug of the personality it speaks through; null when it declares none

qos.description: Its scheduling priority and model fallbacks, as declared; null is business priority with no fallbacks

routines.description: The routines it holds, in declared order; a gathered agent's are sorted by name

routing.description: "Ask me about...": when people and other agents should come to it. Empty when not declared

signedAt.description: When the latest version was signed, as an ISO-8601 instant string; null when it has never been signed

signedBy.description: Username of whoever signed the latest version; null when it has never been signed

sponsor.description: Username of the person who answers for it: as declared, else as recorded when someone adopted it; null while nobody has, which keeps it off duty

stage.description: The stage chosen for the agent: off, observing or on. A stage set through POST /agents/{name}/stage overrides the declared one; what actually fires is each routine's `firing`

state.description: Lifecycle state: draft, submitted, active, suspended or retired. Only an active agent goes on duty; retired is final

sweeps.description: The cold materializations it keeps filled, as declared. Each one buys producer fetches and model judgements for as long as it runs, so this is what a sponsor signs for

unsignedChanges.description: What the world holds now that the signed version does not, one sentence per change. Dispatch runs the signed version, so none of these take effect until it is signed again

version.description: Its latest signed version; 0 for an agent never signed, or one gathered from routines

AnnotateDryRunRequest.description: An annotation statement to freeze into a plan, writing nothing; the body of POST /admin/kg/annotations/dry-run

params.description: Values for the statement's $parameters, by name, resolved when the plan freezes; empty when absent

statement.description: One Cypher annotation statement: a read prefix (MATCH, OPTIONAL MATCH, WITH), then WITH DISTINCT <target>[, <expr> AS <alias>] ORDER BY ... LIMIT n, then SET <target>.<property> = <literal | $parameter | alias>. The property must be one the world's annotatable declarations allow on the target's label

AnswerBoundary.description: Marks a query result whose rows are not an answer: the original filter matched nothing, and what came back is a card of already-fetched facts about the pinned record. Carried as `answerBoundary`.

kind.description: What the rows are instead of an answer. Only SUPPORTING_CONTEXT_ONLY exists.

unresolvedQuestion.description: The question the rows do not answer: the asked question on `/ask`, `view:<name>` on a view run. Null on `/execute`, which has no question.

AnswerRequest.description: A person's answer to one open question, sent to POST /learn/{id}/answer

choice.description: The value of one of that question's options (OptionWire.value), e.g. `keep`, `reverse` or `accept`

subject.description: The question's subject, as QuestionWire.subject gives it

ApiError.description: A refusal with a machine-readable code and a plain-language message. ApiErrorAdvice answers it for a failed validation, a missing resource or a conflicting state, and some controllers answer it directly

code.description: Machine-readable key to branch on, such as validation_failed, unknown_field, not_found or conflict. Open: a surface may answer codes of its own

detail.description: Extra context where there is some, such as the fields a body may carry; null otherwise

message.description: A plain-language explanation, written to be shown. Never carries an exception message

ApiModesResponse.description: How an API may authenticate when connected, answered by GET /learn/apis/modes

modes.description: Each auth mode, as id, label and the form that connects with it; the id goes in ConnectApiRequest.mode

ApprovalRequest.description: Decisions a person approves, sent to POST /learn/{id}/approval. Approvals are recorded and shown, not yet enforced

revision.description: The revision the approver read; one that is no longer current is refused 409 REVISION_STALE

subjects.description: Subjects of displayed decisions, e.g. `rename:Grant`. An empty list, or a subject the review does not display, is refused 400 DECISION_UNKNOWN

name.description: The artifact's name

type.description: The ArtifactType name, upper case, as resolved from the request's case-insensitive type

ArtifactDeleted.description: Confirmation that an artifact was deleted

name.description: The artifact's name

ArtifactError.description: A refusal carrying only its reason

error.description: Why the request was refused, written to be shown

ArtifactListing.description: Every artifact in the world, grouped by type

artifacts.description: Artifacts by lower-case ArtifactType name. Every type is present, carrying an empty list when it holds nothing

ArtifactSummary.description: One artifact as the listings describe it: its identity, size, provenance and, for an app, where it is served

createdAt.description: When it was created, ISO-8601. Null where the filesystem does not expose creation time

createdBy.description: Who or what created it. Null for artifacts older than change tracking

description.description: The artifact's own description where it declares one, null where it does not

iconUrl.description: Where this app's icon is served from. Null for non-apps and for the many apps that declare no icon — a client keeps whatever it drew before

lastModified.description: When this artifact was last written, ISO-8601

lastModifiedBy.description: Who or what most recently wrote it

name.description: The artifact's name, unique within its type

readOnly.description: True for an artifact from a read-only source — a world template or an installed realm — which cannot be edited or deleted here

scope.description: The URL scope an app is served under: the workspace, the world, or a realm name. Non-app artifacts carry the default

servable.description: True when this artifact's TYPE can be served as files, which is a property of the type and not of this artifact

url.description: Where an app is served from. Null for every artifact that is not an app

ArtifactValidationFailure.description: A write refused because the content did not validate

error.description: Always `Validation failed`; the detail is in violations

ArtifactWritten.description: Confirmation that an artifact was created or replaced

name.description: The artifact's name

size.description: The stored content's length in characters, which is not necessarily its size in bytes

AskRequest.description: Body of `POST /documents/ask`: a question for the caller's own documents, and what narrows the search.

answer.description: False to skip composing an answer and return sources only, from a deterministic search with no language-model call. Defaults to true.

history.description: Prior turns, oldest first, each a `Q:` line followed by an `A:` line, so a follow-up needs no session. Only the last 6 are used, and only when an answer is composed.

intent.description: A brief for the retrieval's judgement. Accepted, but not currently read by either retrieval path.

maxSnippet.description: Cap on each returned passage, in characters. Defaults to 400 and is clamped to 400..8000; raise it to get whole chunks back, as span-scored retrieval evaluation needs.

minScore.description: Lowest similarity score, 0 to 1, a chunk must reach to count. Read on the sources-only path (`answer` false) only, where it defaults to 0.25.

question.description: The question to answer, or on the sources-only path the text to search for. A blank question is answered 400.

tag.description: Narrow to documents carrying this tag, whether or not an answer is composed.

topK.description: Most documents to return. Defaults to 6; clamped to 1..25.

uri.description: Narrow to the one document at this uri, as GET /documents lists it, whether or not an answer is composed. A uri the caller's world does not hold is answered 404.

window.description: Bounds the search by one of the document's dates. Absent means no date bound.

AskResponse.description: What `POST /documents/ask` answers: the composed answer, the documents it came from, and what constrained the search.

answer.description: The composed answer alone, without the passages the model quoted before it. Null when `answer` was false, when nothing was retrieved, and on a 400 or 404.

filters.description: What constrained the search, echoed back: `dateField`, `from`, `to`, `tag` and `uri` when given, and `topK`; then the effort behind it: `documents` (also as `retrieved`), `chunks` and `searches`. On a 400 or 404, only `error`, with the reason.

model.description: The model this endpoint composes answers with (the world's agentic-RAG role, not the chat model). Reported even when no answer was composed; null on a 400 or 404.

note.description: Why there is no answer, set only when the model was asked to answer and returned no text. Null otherwise, including when nothing matched.

raw.description: Exactly what the model composed, quoted passages and all, before the server split out `answer`. Null when no answer was composed.

sources.description: The documents retrieved, in retrieval order, numbered by `n`. Empty when nothing matched.

unresolvedCitations.description: Citation markers removed because they named no retrieved document. Currently always 0: sources are taken from the retrieval the server observed, not from markers in the answer.

Attachment.description: A typed thing from the world attached to a thread message — a record, a view's rows, or a request — frozen when the message was sent, so the receiver gets the thing rather than a paragraph about it

args.description: For a view, the arguments it ran with; empty otherwise

capturedAt.description: When the attachment was resolved and frozen, as an ISO-8601 instant; null on one an agent attached without a time

id.description: The entity's key or id, or the request's id; null for a view

kind.description: ENTITY for a record, VIEW for a view's rows, REQUEST for a request awaiting or past a person's decision

label.description: The entity's label, the view's name, or request for a request

properties.description: For an entity, the record's properties as the sender saw it; for a request, its verb, status (lowercase), routine and args; empty for a view

rows.description: For a view, its rows as run when the message was sent, at most 25; empty otherwise

title.description: Card title for a person to read; defaults to the label and id for an entity, the view's name for a view, and the request's detail for a request

AttachmentAccepted.description: A file stored and linked to the conversation. What happens to it next is up to dispatch

attachmentId.description: The stored attachment's id, which a later answer may name

filename.description: The file's name as uploaded, or `attachment` where it had none

mimeType.description: The file's media type as uploaded, or application/octet-stream where it had none

AttachmentActivity.description: What has happened to one file attached to this world: the handler that took it, whether its import is running, done or failed, and what it reported. Listed newest first by GET /chat/attachments

filename.description: The file's name as it was attached

finishedAt.description: ISO-8601 instant the import finished or failed; null while importing

handler.description: Name of the handler that took the file

stale.description: True for an `IMPORTING` record started more than 15 minutes ago: most likely a process killed mid-import, not an import still running

summary.description: The handler's own account of what it imported, or for `FAILED` the reason it gave; up to 2,000 characters, empty while importing

AttachmentAnswerOutcome.description: What became of an answer to an attachment question. `status` names the outcome

AttachmentRefusal.description: A refusal from the attachment endpoints: the word `error` and the reason, written to be shown

message.description: Why the file or the answer was refused: an empty or oversized file, or no active chat session

AttachmentRequest.description: Something to attach to a thread message, part of the body of POST /threads/{id}/messages. It is resolved when the message is posted: an entity is taken as given, a view is run, a request is read; one that cannot be resolved is dropped.

args.description: For a view, the arguments to run it with; ignored otherwise

id.description: For an entity, its key or id; for a request, the id of the request to read (required); ignored for a view

kind.description: ENTITY, VIEW or REQUEST, matched case-insensitively

label.description: For an entity, its label; for a view, the name of the view to run; ignored for a request

properties.description: For an entity, the record's properties as the sender sees them; ignored otherwise

title.description: Card title; blank defaults to the label and id for an entity, the view's name for a view, and the request's detail for a request

AuthoritySpec.description: An agent's authority: for each verb that changes something, whether it may act, must ask a person first (request), or may never call it. Verbs that only read are never governed

default.description: Level for every effect not named in `verbs`: act (the default), request or never. An unrecognised level reads as request

observe.description: Gatekeeper rules it only tries: authority, sensitive, egress or review. Each is evaluated and recorded on the run, but the call goes through

reach.description: Namespaces its routines may reach. When set, a call to any API or MCP server not listed is refused, read or write; reading the world's graph and raising a request never are. Null reaches everything

review.description: Whether an independent reviewer reads each write it may make on its own first, and may refuse it; a model call per write. False by default

verbs.description: Level by verb, named as the gateway names it (for example odoo_partnerMessagePost): act, request or never

AvailableSourcesResponse.description: The sources the Get-to-Know-Me flow knows, answered by GET /onboarding/sources

sources.description: Every known source, available or not, in a fixed order

BoltAbout.description: The Bolt server: the ports Neo4j drivers and tools connect to.

endpoints.description: Each port that is listening, Virtual Cypher first

BoltEndpointAbout.description: One Bolt port, as a Neo4j driver or Neo4j Browser dials it.

address.description: The address the server advertises for this port, host:port

answers.description: What that database answers, in a sentence

database.description: The database a session on this port gets when it names none

mode.description: What a session on this port runs against when it names no database

tls.description: Whether the port speaks TLS, so the URL is bolt+s:// rather than bolt://

BootstrapCapabilities.description: Feature flags reported by the bootstrap call

apiDiscoveryEnabled.description: True when the LLM-driven "describe an API in words" discovery flow is switched on. A client should not offer that path otherwise

workosEnabled.description: True when WorkOS AuthKit login is switched on and a client registration for it exists

BootstrapResponse.description: What a fresh client needs before it can talk to the app: how to log in, and who, if anyone, is signed in. Answered by GET /bootstrap, which needs no authentication

capabilities.description: Feature flags a client can act on

currentUser.description: The signed-in user, or null for an anonymous caller

licence.description: The appliance's trial or licence, readable before sign-in so the sign-in screen can say why a locked appliance is paused. Null on a server with no licence gate

preferredLogin.description: The scheme to lead with interactively: `workos-oidc` when WorkOS login is wired, otherwise `session-form`

schemaVersion.description: Version of this response's shape, bumped when a field is removed or changes meaning; additive fields do not bump it. Currently 1

supportedAuthSchemes.description: Auth schemes this deployment accepts: `session-form` and `basic` always, `workos-oidc` when WorkOS login is wired

BootstrapUser.description: The user a bootstrap call found signed in

displayName.description: The human-friendly name; null when no user record exists for the username

BriefingLensRequest.description: Optional window for POST /lenses/briefing. Each field present is passed to the world's briefing lens as the argument of the same name; with none, the lens uses its own default window (30 days in the default world).

asOf.description: ISO-8601 date or instant passed to the lens as asOf; it has effect only if the world's briefing lens reads it, which the default one does not

lookbackDays.description: Number of days back from now the brief covers when since is absent. Null leaves it to the lens.

since.description: ISO-8601 date or instant to brief since; the default briefing lens prefers it over lookbackDays. Null leaves it to the lens.

BrowserLocationRequest.description: A browser geolocation fix, as `navigator.geolocation` reports it, pushed for the signed-in user by POST /context/observation/location

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90; a value outside that range drops the push without recording it

lng.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, -180 to 180; a value outside that range drops the push without recording it

BrowserTimeZoneRequest.description: The browser's time zone, pushed by POST /context/timezone to keep the signed-in user's stored time zone in step with it

zone.description: Time zone id as the browser reports it, normally IANA such as `Europe/London`. Blank, or not an id `java.time.ZoneId` accepts, it is ignored and the stored zone is left as it was

BudgetSpec.description: An agent's hard limits. Each null limit is no limit. Reaching a per-day limit stands the agent down until somebody puts it back; per-run and per-hour limits refuse the run or the call and leave it on duty

concurrentRuns.description: Most of its runs that may be in progress at once

expiresOn.description: ISO-8601 date (yyyy-MM-dd), read in the user's zone, after which it stands down until re-signed with a later one. A date that does not parse stands it down too

requestsPerRun.description: Most requests for people to approve that one run may raise

runsPerHour.description: Most runs it may start in any rolling hour; skipped runs do not count

sourceShares.description: Percent of each source's declared rate it may take, keyed by bucket (a producer's cost.bucket, else its name), with * for every bucket not named. Only sources that declare a rate are paced

spendPerDayCents.description: Most model spend across a day, in US cents

spendPerRunCents.description: Most model spend one run may make, in US cents

writesPerDay.description: Most writes it may make on its own in a day

BuildSnapshot.description: Realm wasm build meters: every attempt to build a realm's handlers bundle, by how it ended

byOutcome.description: One entry per build outcome, sorted by outcome; every outcome is registered at zero, so entries with count 0 are normal

recorded.description: False when the build meters exist but no build attempt has been recorded yet, which tells nothing-happened-yet apart from nothing-records-this

wasmBytes.description: Size of the published handlers.wasm per build attempt that ended with a bundle on disk, in bytes; null only when the meter is not registered

CalendarAccount.description: The connected calendar account an event was read from. Carried on CalendarEvent.account.

accountId.description: The provider's stable identifier for the account, typically its email address

displayName.description: Label recorded for the account when it was connected, for showing in a UI

provider.description: Key of the OAuth provider the account was connected through, such as `google-workspace`

CalendarConnectionsView.description: The calendar providers this server knows and the calendar accounts the signed-in user has connected, answered by GET /calendar/connections. Never carries a credential

accounts.description: The signed-in user's connected calendar accounts, across every provider

providers.description: Every calendar provider registered on this server, whether or not it is configured for connecting

CalendarEvent.description: One instance of an event on a calendar of the signed-in user's connected accounts; a recurring meeting arrives as one entry per occurrence. Returned in the events list of GET /calendar/events.

account.description: The connected account the event was read from; set on every event GET /calendar/events returns

attendees.description: Everyone invited, people and resources alike; empty when the event has no guest list

calendarId.description: The provider's id of the calendar holding the event; one account can have several calendars

description.description: Event description or agenda as the provider stores it, which may contain HTML; empty when there is none

end.description: End of the event, an ISO-8601 instant, exclusive; one hour after start when the provider gave no end

eventId.description: The provider's id for this event instance

isAllDay.description: True for an all-day event, which has a date but no time of day

isRecurring.description: True when this is one occurrence of a recurring series

joinUrl.description: Video-call link: the provider's structured conference link, else a legacy Meet link, else the first http(s) URL in the location; null when none is found

location.description: Location text as the provider gives it, a place name or an address; null when absent or blank

myResponse.description: The signed-in user's reply, from their own attendee entry. With no such entry it is ACCEPTED when the event has no guests or they organized or created it, otherwise NEEDS_ACTION

organizer.description: The organizer, from the provider's organizer field or else the attendee marked as organizer; null when there is neither

start.description: Start of the event, an ISO-8601 instant. For an all-day event, midnight at the start of its date in the event's time zone

timeZone.description: Time-zone id the event is scheduled in, such as `Europe/London`, for display; the calendar's own zone when the event names none or an unknown one

title.description: Event title; `(no title)` when the provider has none

url.description: Link to the event in the provider's web UI; null when the provider gives none

visibility.description: The provider's visibility setting for the event; DEFAULT when it sets none or a value not listed

CapabilitiesRequest.description: The sensor's whole verb catalog for the consent groups its user has enabled. It replaces the one published before

verbs.description: Every verb the machine now offers. Empty or absent withdraws them all. The appliance offers them only while the sensor keeps polling the outbox

CatchupRefusal.description: A catchup run that was refused or failed. Carries only the reason

error.description: Why: the unknown username, or the failure the pipeline reported

CatchupRunReport.description: What one on-demand catchup run did for a user

durationMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the run in milliseconds

notifications.description: How many notifications the run produced

signals.description: How many in-window signals the run fanned through triage

username.description: The user the run was for, as requested

Change.description: One proposed change to an agent: what it targets, the new value, and the reason and evidence for it

duty.description: The duty to add when target is "add-duty"; null otherwise

evidence.description: The counts from the record that support the change, as the model cited them

from.description: The current value, as the model stated it; not checked against the agent, and null when the model gave none

target.description: What the change touches: "job", "routing", "persona", "duty:<name>:text", "duty:<name>:every" (an existing duty), or "add-duty" (with duty)

to.description: The new value: text for job, routing, persona and duty text, a six-field cron for a duty's cadence; ignored for add-duty

why.description: The model's reason for the change

ChangeRequest.description: A person's own words for one displayed name or description, sent to POST /learn/{id}/change

revision.description: The revision the person read; one that is no longer current is refused 409 REVISION_STALE

subject.description: The subject of a displayed rename or description decision, e.g. `rename:Grant`; any other kind is refused 400 CHANGE_INVALID, and one not displayed 400 DECISION_UNKNOWN

value.description: The new value, trimmed: for a rename, one word of letters, digits and underscores starting with a letter; for a description, its whole text. Empty or unchanged is refused 400 CHANGE_INVALID

ChannelsResponse.description: The audience channels this world offers and the ones the acting user has joined. Answered by `GET /audience/channels` and, after the change, by `PUT /audience/channels`.

joined.description: The channels the acting user has joined, sorted by name; may include channels nothing currently declares

offered.description: Every channel a view or app in this world declares, whether or not anybody has joined it, sorted by name. Empty when the world could not be loaded

ChatCompletion.description: An agent's answer in OpenAI's chat.completion shape, answered by the chat completions endpoints when stream is not true

choices.description: Exactly one choice, holding the agent's answer

created.description: When the turn started, in Unix epoch seconds

embabel.description: What the turn did; present only when the request set embabel_evidence

id.description: chatcmpl- followed by a random UUID, new for every completion

model.description: Name of the agent that answered

ChatCompletionRequest.description: An OpenAI chat completion request to an agent, sent to POST /openai/v1/chat/completions or /agents/{name}/v1/chat/completions. Fields OpenAI defines and this does not list (tools, top_p…) are ignored; the embabel_ fields are this server's own.

embabel_conversation.description: Conversation name the caller chooses: the same name, from any client, continues the same conversation with this agent. Absent or blank, the conversation is recognised from the user and how the history began.

embabel_evidence.description: True adds the embabel evidence object to the response (on the final chunk when streaming); otherwise it is absent

embabel_observing.description: True refuses every effect the agent attempts this turn, even if it is on duty, and reports what it would have done

embabel_realms.description: Realm names to narrow the conversation to, from among the agent's own; never adds one. Absent or empty keeps all of them.

embabel_verbosity.description: Reply length: terse asks for a sentence or two, full for a full answer, normal (or absent, or any other value) for neither. Case-insensitive.

max_completion_tokens.description: Reply length cap in tokens, preferred over max_tokens; capped at the agent's declared most, ignored when it declares none

max_tokens.description: Reply length cap in tokens, used when max_completion_tokens is absent; capped at the agent's declared most, ignored when it declares none

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first, as OpenAI clients resend it each time. The newest user message is the turn answered; earlier user and assistant messages are context. At least one non-blank user message is required.

model.description: Name of the agent to talk to, as listed by GET /openai/v1/models; ignored on an agent's own base URL, where the path names the agent

stream.description: True answers as server-sent chat.completion.chunk events ending in [DONE]; the whole answer arrives as one content chunk. Absent or false answers one chat.completion.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, clamped into the range the agent declares; ignored when the agent declares none

user.description: The client's own end-user id, when it sends one; part of how a conversation is recognised, so two of its users' chats stay apart

model.description: The pinned chat model, or null when chat inherits one

reasoningEffort.description: The reasoning effort chat runs at, or null for the model's default

temperature.description: The sampling temperature, or null for the model's default

ChatErrorRefusal.description: A refusal carrying only its reason, with no status word

error.description: Why the request was refused, written to be shown

ChatFeedbackRequest.description: A thumbs up or down on an assistant reply already received; the body of POST /chat/feedback

text.description: Text of the assistant reply being judged; blank is a 400

verdict.description: up or down, case-insensitive; anything else is a 400

ChatModelUpdated.description: The model chat now uses, with any role pin cleared

inherited.description: True when no model is pinned, so chat uses the deployment default

model.description: The model now pinned, trimmed; null or blank when chat went back to inheriting

ChatProcessKilled.description: A process that was running and has been killed

previousStatus.description: The process's status at the moment it was killed, such as RUNNING or WAITING

ChatRequest.description: A user message for the open chat session; the body of POST /chat. The reply arrives on the SSE stream

message.description: The user's message text, sent to the assistant as their turn

ChatSessionDeleted.description: A chat session that has been deleted, with whether it was the one the live stream was attached to

wasActive.description: True when this was the session attached to the caller's live chat stream, which is detached too — a client should leave it for a blank chat

ChatStatusRefusal.description: A refusal from the chat surface: the word `error` and the reason, written to be shown

message.description: What was refused and why, such as no open stream, no active session, or an unknown command

status.description: Always `error`. A client may branch on it rather than on the status code

Choice.description: One answer in a chat completion; there is only ever one

message.description: The agent's answer

CodeActionCatalog.description: Every realm API operation available to a user, counted per source, with a sample

bySource.description: The operations counted per source realm, keyed by source name in sorted order

sample.description: Up to twenty operations, sorted by gateway name

totalRealmOps.description: How many realm API operations the user can reach

username.description: The user the catalog was built for, as given

CodeActionCatalogOp.description: One realm API operation, as the catalog samples it

readOnly.description: True when the operation only reads

source.description: The realm the operation comes from

CodeActionResumed.description: A process resumed from its confirmation gate

accepted.description: Whether the write was approved. A rejected write's commit step never runs

awaitingConfirmation.description: True when the process has parked again at another gate — a plan with several writes asks once per write

status.description: The process's status after resuming, such as COMPLETED or WAITING

CodeActionSourceCount.description: One source's operations, split by whether they only read

write.description: The operations classified as writes: total less readOnly

ColleaguesSpec.description: An agent's half of consent between colleagues: whom it may message, and who may message it. A message goes through only when both agents agree

mayBeMessagedBy.description: Names of the agents that may message it

mayMessage.description: Names of the agents it may message

CollectorConfig.description: This world's overrides for the memory-dedup sweep that collapses near-duplicate propositions. Each non-null field replaces the deployment default; null inherits it. Part of GET /config; GET /config/collector answers the resolved values

cron.description: Six-field Spring cron (seconds first) for the sweep; null inherits the deployment default. Stored and reported, but the scheduled sweep runs on the deployment cron, so this does not change when it runs

dryRun.description: When true, a sweep reports what it would collapse but changes nothing; null inherits the deployment default

enabled.description: Whether the sweep runs for this world; null inherits the deployment default (off unless the operator turned it on)

entityOverlap.description: Multi-signal weight, 0 to 1, of overlap between the entities two propositions mention; null uses the matcher's own default. Used only with the multi-signal matcher

groundingOverlap.description: Multi-signal weight, 0 to 1, of overlap between the sources two propositions are grounded in; null uses the matcher's own default. Used only with the multi-signal matcher

lexical.description: Multi-signal weight, 0 to 1, of lexical (wording) similarity; null uses the matcher's own default. Used only with the multi-signal matcher

matcher.description: How duplicates are decided: cosine (embedding similarity alone) or multi-signal (a weighted blend of the five signals below); null inherits the deployment default

provenanceOverlap.description: Multi-signal weight, 0 to 1, of overlap in where two propositions came from; null uses the matcher's own default. Used only with the multi-signal matcher

similarityThreshold.description: Similarity floor, 0 to 1, at which two propositions cluster as near-duplicates; null inherits the deployment default

vector.description: Multi-signal weight, 0 to 1, of embedding similarity; null uses the matcher's own default. Used only with the multi-signal matcher

CollectorSettingsRequest.description: Body of PUT /config/collector: every memory-dedup collector setting for this world, replacing what is stored. The five signal weights are top-level fields.

cron.description: When the sweep runs, as a Spring six-field cron expression (seconds minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week)

dryRun.description: Whether the sweep reports what it would merge instead of merging it

enabled.description: Whether the dedup sweep runs at all

matcher.description: Which matcher decides that two memories are the same: `cosine` or `multi-signal`

similarityThreshold.description: How similar two memories must be to merge, in [0, 1]

CollectorSettingsView.description: The memory-dedup collector settings in force for this world. The first five are resolved against the deployment defaults and are never null; the five weights are returned as stored, where null means the matcher's own default applies.

cron.description: When the sweep runs, as a Spring six-field cron expression

dryRun.description: Whether the sweep reports what it would merge instead of merging it

enabled.description: Whether the dedup sweep runs at all

entityOverlap.description: Weight of shared entities. Null means the matcher's own default

groundingOverlap.description: Weight of shared grounding. Null means the matcher's own default

lexical.description: Weight of lexical overlap. Null means the matcher's own default

matcher.description: Which matcher decides that two memories are the same

provenanceOverlap.description: Weight of shared provenance. Null means the matcher's own default

similarityThreshold.description: How similar two memories must be to merge, in [0, 1]

vector.description: Weight of vector similarity. Null means the matcher's own default

CommandRunRequest.description: Optional body of POST /chat/command/{command}: the text that follows the slash command

argument.description: Text appended after /<command> and a space; null or blank runs the command with no argument

CompileAndScheduleRequest.description: A job described in words, the body of POST /cron/compile: compiled into an action named `cron-<name>`, then scheduled

cron.description: Spring 6-field cron expression (seconds minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week), evaluated in the user's time zone. Not validated here: an unparseable one is saved but never fires

description.description: What the job should do, in natural language. Compiled into the action's prompt, and kept as the job's description

inputTypeNames.description: Domain types the compiled action takes as inputs; absent means none

name.description: Job name. The compiled action is saved as `cron-<name>`, and a job of the same name is replaced

outputTypeName.description: Domain type the compiled action produces; absent or blank means a `BackgroundMessage`

toolNames.description: Tools the compiled action may call; absent means none

CompileRequest.description: The body of POST /actions/compile: a description an LLM turns into a prompted action, saved to the world's config/actions directory.

description.description: What the action should do, in natural language; the LLM writes the prompt template from it, and it is kept as the action's description

inputTypeNames.description: Types the action takes as input, by name from GET /actions/available-types; each becomes a template variable named after the type's simple name in lower camel case. Omitted means none

llmModel.description: Model the action runs on, which also writes its template; omitted uses the platform's default model

llmTemperature.description: Sampling temperature the action runs at; 0.0 when omitted. Writing the template uses 0.1 when this is 0 or less

name.description: Name of the action and of its file, `config/actions/<name>.yml`; a world action already saved under that name is overwritten

outputTypeName.description: Type the action produces, by name; omitted or blank means `com.embabel.agent.spec.model.BackgroundMessage`

referenceNames.description: Skills, reference documents or memory the action may draw on, by name from GET /actions/available-references; omitted means none

toolNames.description: Tools the action may call, by name from GET /actions/available-tools; omitted means none

CompileScheduleRequest.description: A schedule described in natural language

schedule.description: The schedule in words, e.g. 'every day at 7am'

ComponentVersion.description: One part of the running server and the build of it that is running.

commit.description: Full git commit SHA, when the component was built with one

name.description: Human name of the component

version.description: Released or snapshot version, when the component carries one

ConfigUpdated.description: A config change was saved. Carries only the acknowledgement — the caller already knows what it sent

ConnectApiRequest.description: How to reach an API, sent to POST /learn/apis: an auth mode and that mode's fields, with the top-level specUrl, name, token and headerName accepted too, for a script that has them in hand

fields.description: Values for the mode's form, keyed by each field's name (`specUrl`, `name`, `token`, `headerName`). A top-level property of the same name takes precedence; blank values count as absent

headerName.description: The header that carries the key, for mode `api-key` only; absent means `X-API-Key`. Not secret

mode.description: An auth-mode id from GET /learn/apis/modes: `none`, `bearer` or `api-key`. Absent means `none`; any other value is refused 400

name.description: The gateway namespace to register the API under, made into a slug; absent uses the spec's own title

specUrl.description: URL of the API's OpenAPI document, fetched to prove it answers. Required, here or as fields.specUrl

token.description: The bearer token or API key, required for modes `bearer` and `api-key`. Stored in the user's wallet, never echoed back and never written to world YAML

ConnectDatabaseRequest.description: How to reach a database, sent to POST /learn/databases: an engine and its form's fields, as a picker sends them, or a JDBC URL a caller already has

engine.description: An engine id from GET /learn/databases/engines, e.g. `postgresql`, `oracle`, `duckdb`. When given, the URL is composed from fields and jdbcUrl is ignored; absent or blank means jdbcUrl is used. An id this appliance has no driver for is refused 400

fields.description: Values for the engine's form, keyed by each field's name, `username` and `password` among them. A blank value takes the field's default; a required field left blank with no default is refused 400. Read only with engine

jdbcUrl.description: A complete JDBC URL, for a caller that has one. Used only when engine is absent or blank, and then required

password.description: Stored in the user's wallet, never echoed back and never written to world YAML. With engine, a non-blank value takes precedence over fields.password; empty means no password

username.description: The login the world reads the database as. With engine, a non-blank value takes precedence over fields.username

ConnectedAccountView.description: One account the signed-in user has connected; it never carries a credential. Listed by GET /email/connections and GET /calendar/connections.

accountId.description: The provider's stable identifier for the account, typically its email address; the id DELETE /email/connections/{accountId} takes

displayName.description: Label recorded for the account when it was connected, for showing in a UI

provider.description: Key of the provider the account was connected through; matches a provider's providerName

ConnectionProviderView.description: A provider this appliance can connect accounts with, and where to start connecting one. Listed by GET /email/connections and GET /calendar/connections.

authorizeUrl.description: Path on this server that starts the provider's OAuth flow; send the browser there to connect an account

configured.description: True when the provider is set up on this appliance, so an account can be connected through it

displayName.description: Name to show for the provider, such as `Google`

providerName.description: Provider key, such as `google-workspace` or `microsoft-graph`; the value a connected account's provider carries

ContextRequest.description: Body of PUT /config/router/contexts/{id}: a role or a model for the context, not both; neither returns it to the deployment default

model.description: The model the context is pinned to

ContextView.description: One context, a job this world uses a model for, with the role or model it is set to and the model that answers it. Part of GET /config/router

deploymentModel.description: The model the deployment's default for this context names; null when that default selects by role, or there is no default

deploymentRole.description: The role the deployment's default for this context selects by; null when that default names a model, or there is no default (the planner, which follows chat, or a context the deployment leaves unset)

followsChat.description: True for the planner when it has no role or model of its own, so it runs on whatever chat runs on, through chat's role; false for every other context

id.description: The context: `chat`, `plannerLlm`, `codingLlm`, `fallbackCodingLlm`, `rankerLlm` or `lensLlm`; the {id} in PUT /config/router/contexts/{id}

model.description: The model this world pinned the context to; null when it pinned none

resolved.description: The model it runs on now; null when nothing can serve it, or when the context names no model at all (a fallback coder with neither a setting nor a default)

role.description: The role this world chose for the context; null when it chose none

roleInUse.description: The role the context reaches its model through, from this world's setting or else the deployment's default; null when it reaches a model without one

ConversationSpec.description: The scope of a conversation with an agent (/talk <name>): the realms it reaches, the host tools it keeps, the LLM role it runs on, and what a caller may ask of sampling

builtins.description: Which host tools it keeps: true or null for all, false for none, or one category name or a list of them. An unknown category is logged and left out

llm.description: The LLM role the conversation runs on, never a model name; null for the default

realms.description: Names of the realms the conversation reaches; empty scopes it to the realm that shipped the agent

sampling.description: Bounds on the sampling a caller may ask for; null leaves the role's own settings

ConversionFailure.description: One document conversion that failed and fell back to flat text extraction, losing headings and tables; listed in the conversion section of GET /admin/system

at.description: When the failure happened, as an ISO-8601 instant

document.description: Filename of the uploaded document; re-ingesting it once the converter is healthy is the remedy

reason.description: The converter's error message, or "no reason given" when it had none

ConversionStatus.description: Which converter turns documents into structured text, and how it is doing

converter.description: The active converter's name; 'none' when documents go straight to flat text extraction

docling.description: Whether docling is the active converter and whether it answers

failuresSinceStart.description: Conversions that failed and fell back to flat text since the app started

recentFailures.description: The most recent of those, newest last

Counts.description: What the agent has done lately, summed over its record in the units a budget is set in

requestsToday.description: Requests it raised today for a person to approve, from the same midnight

runsLastHour.description: Runs started in the last hour, skipped firings excluded, counted over its 500 most recent runs

writesToday.description: Changes it made today: receipts where a call acted, plus requests a person approved. Today starts at midnight in the user's time zone, UTC when they have none

CpuStatus.description: CPU load, as fractions of what this JVM may use

processLoad.description: This app's share of the CPU it may use, 0.0–1.0. Null when not yet measured.

systemLoad.description: The whole machine's load, 0.0–1.0 — in a container, the container's quota. Null when not yet measured.

CreateLensRequest.description: A lens to save for the caller; sent to PUT /lenses, which answers the saved lens's id and name

name.description: Display name, required and non-blank. The lens id is derived from it (lowercased, each run of other characters turned into -), so saving under a name with the same id replaces that lens.

params.description: Parameters the lens accepts when it is opened, supplied then in the args map; empty for none

persona.description: Persona slug stored with the lens and returned with its definition; null for none

schedule.description: Cron expression stored with the lens; nothing schedules from it yet, so it has no effect

script.description: CypherScript program, required and non-blank: code-mode JavaScript that queries through gateway.kg.query and other gateway calls and declares its focus with gateway.lens.focus

CreatePersonalityRequest.description: Body of POST /world/personalities: a new world-tier personality, blank or duplicated from an existing one

from.description: Slug of a personality, world or realm tier, whose files to copy; null for a blank personality

name.description: Display name, written into the personality's identity.yml

slug.description: Identifier of the new personality, trimmed: a lowercase letter or digit, then up to 39 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. Refused when taken

CreateSkillRequest.description: Body of POST /world/skills: a new local skill, written as a SKILL.md following the Agent Skills Specification

description.description: What the skill does and when to use it, at most 1024 characters; the SKILL.md front matter's description

instructions.description: Markdown instructions the assistant follows when using the skill; the SKILL.md body

name.description: Skill name and directory: 1-64 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen, e.g. `research-helper`

CreateThreadRequest.description: A thread to start; sent to POST /threads

title.description: Title for the thread, trimmed; blank or absent makes it "Untitled"

CreateWatchRequest.description: The body of POST /watches: which saved lens to watch with what arguments, when to run it, and how to compare and deliver what changes.

cron.description: Spring cron expression, six fields with seconds first (such as `0 0 8 * * *`), evaluated in the server's time zone. Omitted or blank, the watch runs only when POST /watches/{watchId}/runs asks

delivery.description: Where each diff is sent: channel `notification` (the inbox), `signal` (the agent bus) or `webhook`. Omitted or null, diffs are kept in the watch's history only

diffSpec.description: How a run's result is compared with the previous complete run's; omitted takes every DiffSpec default

enabled.description: False creates the watch switched off, so it is not scheduled and runs are refused; true when omitted

firstRunPolicy.description: ESTABLISH_BASELINE (the default): the first run records what the lens shows and produces no diff. EMIT_CURRENT: the first run is diffed against nothing, so everything it finds is reported

lensId.description: Id of the saved lens to watch; it must be one the signed-in user can open

name.description: Label for the watch; the lensId when omitted or blank

params.description: Arguments given to the lens on every run, by parameter name; empty runs it on its defaults

name.description: The world's name; no slashes and no '..'

CronJobConfig.description: A scheduled job in the user's world that runs a world action on a cron schedule. GET /cron lists the active ones; POST /cron takes one to create or replace.

actionName.description: World action the job runs when it fires. A job saved with this blank is not scheduled again when the world's cron configs are reloaded.

cron.description: Spring 6-field cron expression (seconds minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week), e.g. 0 0 9 * * *. An unparseable expression is saved but never fires.

description.description: What the job does, in prose; carried on the cron event the action receives

name.description: Job key, unique within the user's world: saved as config/cron/<name>.yml, and saving a job under an existing name replaces it

payload.description: Values handed to the action on the cron event at every firing; empty by default

zone.description: IANA zone the cron expression is read in, e.g. Australia/Sydney. Null means the owning user's own zone; an invalid zone is logged and the user's zone used instead.

DataContractBindingSpec.description: A view's version-pinned reference to one object in an ODCS data contract the world holds: a view's `dataContract`

id.description: Id of the ODCS contract; must not be blank

mode.description: `observe` (the default): rows are returned and the verdict reported beside them. `enforce`: rows are withheld when the verdict is `FAIL` or `UNKNOWN`, and the contract must be `active` or `deprecated` to run at all

object.description: The schema object in the contract the view's rows are checked against, by name or else physical name; must not be blank

version.description: The contract version pinned; must not be blank. Only the contract with exactly this id and version governs the view

DataContractCheck.description: One check made when a view's result was evaluated against its data contract

message.description: What it found, in words, naming rows and fields but never their values; null when there is nothing to say

ruleId.description: The contract's own id for a quality or freshness rule, or an `embabel:` id for a check the runtime makes itself, such as `embabel:schema`, `embabel:binding` or `embabel:status`

scope.description: `invocation` for the schema check, which covers this one result; null for every other check

verdict.description: `PASS`, `WARN`, `FAIL`, or `UNKNOWN` when the check could not be made

DataContractEvaluation.description: Evidence that one named view's result was checked against its pinned data contract: the verdict, each check, and whether the rows were withheld. Carried as `dataContract` on the result of a view bound to a contract

apiVersion.description: The ODCS apiVersion the contract declares, such as `v3.1.0`; `v3.1.0` when the view was refused before it ran

available.description: False when the view could not run under its contract: the pinned contract or its object is missing, or its status forbids it. Then no rows are returned, whatever the mode

checkedAt.description: ISO-8601 instant the result was checked

checks.description: Each check made, in the order it was made

id.description: Id of the governing contract, as the view's binding pins it

object.description: The contract object the rows were checked against, as the binding names it

status.description: The contract's ODCS status, such as `active`, `deprecated` or `retired`; `unavailable` when the pinned contract is not in the world

verdict.description: The worst of the checks: `FAIL` if any failed, else `UNKNOWN` if any could not be made, else `WARN` if any warned, else `PASS`

DateWindow.description: A date bound on a document search: which of the document's dates to bound, and the range.

field.description: Which date to bound: `modified` (the default, the document's own last-changed date), `created`, or `ingested`. An unrecognised value applies no date bound.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound, as a date (`2026-01-01`) or an ISO-8601 instant.

to.description: Exclusive upper bound, in the same forms as `from`.

DecisionRequest.description: The owner's decision on an agent's request, the body of `POST /requests/{id}/decision`.

decision.description: `approve` or `reject`, case-insensitive. Approving calls the request's verb as the caller.

reason.description: Why the request is rejected, recorded on it and in the run ledger. Required, and not blank, for `reject`; ignored for `approve`.

DecisionResponse.description: The outcome of a decision: the request as it now stands (200), or why the decision was refused (409).

refused.description: Why the decision was refused: already decided or expired, a rejection with no reason, or a decision other than approve/reject. Null when it was applied.

request.description: The request after the decision — APPROVED, REJECTED, or FAILED when the approved verb call failed. Null when the decision was refused.

DeliverySpec.description: Where a watch sends each diff it detects: the inbox, the signal bus, or a webhook. A watch with none keeps its diffs in its history only

channel.description: The adapter: `notification` (the inbox, the default), `signal` (the bus, for agents) or `webhook` (a URL). A lowercase adapter id

format.description: A webhook's body: `json` (the whole diff, the default) or `slack` (a text summary an incoming webhook shows as-is)

headers.description: Extra headers sent on every webhook delivery, e.g. an `Authorization`. At most 16; `X-World-*` and `Content-Type` cannot be set. Values are write-only: a read masks each, and an update that sends a mask back keeps that value

secret.description: When set, a webhook body is signed with HMAC-SHA256 under it, sent as `X-World-Signature: sha256=<hex>`. Write-only: a read returns `••••••••`, and an update that sends that back keeps the stored secret

tier.description: The inbox tier a `notification` delivery is filed at: AMBIENT (the default), DEFERRED, TIMELY, INTERRUPTIVE, ACTING or ESCALATING, case-insensitive; anything else files as AMBIENT. Read by no other channel

url.description: The http(s) URL a `webhook` delivery is POSTed to. Required for `webhook`; unused otherwise

DeploymentUse.description: A model setting the deployment makes under `assistant.infrastructure`, which no world can change yet; listed in GET /config/router as deploymentUses

model.description: The model it names; null when it selects by role rather than by name

role.description: The LLM role it selects its model through; null when it does not select by role

setting.description: Where it is configured: the property path under `assistant.infrastructure`, by Kotlin property name (camelCase)
