choices.description: The question a parked run poses to its owner.

cypher.description: The Cypher the run executes, as submitted to `/execute` after any parameter substitution.

detail.description: Why the run ended as it did, when anything was recorded.

endedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the run settled. Absent while running or parked.

expiresAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which a parked run lapses into EXPIRED.

result.description: The query result. Present only when `state` is COMPLETED.

runId.description: The run id from the path, echoed back.

startedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the run started.

state.description: RUNNING, WAITING_INPUT (parked on `choices`), or one of the settled states COMPLETED, KILLED, FAILED, CANCELLED or EXPIRED.

KgSaveViewRejection.description: A view was refused: a bad name, an unrunnable body, or a name already taken.

error.description: Why the view was refused. Always present.

name.description: The requested name, trimmed. Absent when the declaration itself was malformed — a reserved or uncoercible param, say — and refused before a save was attempted.

violations.description: Preflight defects when the body names shapes the schema contradicts.

KgSaveViewRequest.description: A user-authored view to save into the acting user's world: the body of `POST /views`.

cypher.description: The view's body. RETURN one node variable for a view that composes as a label, or a projection for a tabular view run directly. Must pass the schema preflight with declared defaults substituted.

description.description: One line on what the view answers, shown to the query generator beside the schema. Defaults to empty.

materialized.description: Cache the result and serve reads from the cache until `ttl` lapses. Defaults false: a regular view re-runs on every read.

name.description: A plain identifier — letters, digits and underscore, not starting with a digit — because a query uses it as a label. Trimmed before it is checked; a name a shipped view owns is refused.

outputLabel.description: The node label the view's rows are, e.g. `Person`. A materialized view with one caches its member nodes; without one it keeps its rows as a snapshot. A regular view does not need it.

params.description: Bind variables the body references as `$name`, by name. A materialized view may declare none.

ttl.description: Cache lifetime for a materialized view, e.g. `30m`, `2h`, `1d`. Absent means `1h`; ignored for a regular view.

name.description: The name the view was saved under — the requested name, trimmed.

note.description: Why the stored query differs from the one sent

ok.description: Always true; a refusal answers 400 with a different body.

savedCypher.description: The stored query, when promotion inlined captured scopes into it

KgSchemaLabel.description: A node label and its sampled property shape.

anchor.description: True when this label may open a MATCH pattern bare — a real read, or a virtual population implicitly bound by user tenancy. False means it is reachable only by traversal from a bound anchor; an editor should not offer it at first position. Defaults true so an older client reading a newer appliance loses nothing.

description.description: The declared definition of the type this label names, verbatim from the realm's own registry — for an editor to show on hover. Null for core/introspected labels, which declare none.

exhaustive.description: True when every node carrying this label was inspected, so an absent property genuinely does not exist here. False means the sample was capped — evidence of what exists, and no evidence at all about what does not.

label.description: The node label, as a MATCH pattern writes it.

properties.description: The properties seen on the sampled nodes. See `exhaustive` for what an absence means.

realm.description: The realm that declared this label's type. Null means core — the world's own types or the host's.

sampleCount.description: How many nodes were sampled when inferring the properties.

KgSchemaProperty.description: A property observed on nodes carrying a label.

alternateKey.description: True when the realm's type declares this property as an ALTERNATE KEY: it identifies the same record as the identity does, in the vocabulary the source's own readers use. A policy's `policy_identifier` is its identity; its `policy_number` is what a view shows and what a client will try to join on. Both name the same policy. Unlike the identity, an alternate key is not the dedupe key and is not required on write, so a type may declare several. Defaults false.

description.description: The property's DECLARED description, verbatim from the realm's registry — for an editor to show on hover. Null where the declaration documents nothing.

identity.description: True when the realm's type declares this property as the node's IDENTITY. Two columns denote the same thing only when both project the identity of the same label; matching names prove nothing, and a client that joins on them will relate records that are not related. Defaults false so an older client reading a newer appliance loses nothing, and so an undeclared property is never mistaken for a key.

name.description: The property key, as a query writes it after the dot.

sparse.description: True when the property was missing from a non-trivial fraction of the sample.

type.description: Inferred type tag: string, long, datetime, list<string>, any, …

KgSchemaRelationship.description: A (from, type, to) triple observed in the world subgraph.

from.description: The label of the node the relationship starts from.

to.description: The label of the node the relationship points to.

KgSchemaResponse.description: Labels, their properties, and relationship triples reachable by the acting user.

labels.description: Every label in the snapshot, virtual ones included. Empty only when there is no snapshot.

refreshedAt.description: When the snapshot was taken, ISO-8601. Absent when there is no snapshot.

relationships.description: The (from, type, to) triples in the snapshot. Empty only when there is no snapshot.

KgScopeDeleteResponse.description: The outcome of deleting a captured scope.

deleted.description: True when a scope was dropped; false when the user had no live scope of that name, which is not an error.

name.description: The scope name from the path, echoed back.

KgScopeInfo.description: A captured query scope: a frozen result set referenced in a later query as (x:`$name`).

expiresAt.description: When the scope lapses, ISO-8601 — null means PINNED (kept until deleted).

members.description: How many members the capture froze. Membership is frozen; values stay live.

name.description: The name the scope was captured under, unique per user; a later query binds it as (x:`$name`).

outputLabel.description: The node label later references bind with.

statement.description: The statement that produced the capture — the scope's provenance.

KgScopeListResponse.description: The acting user's live captured scopes, newest first.

scopes.description: The live scopes, newest first; an expired scope is absent.

KgUnknownScopeResponse.description: The named scope does not exist in the acting user's world; the ones that do travel with the refusal.

available.description: The scope names this world declares (its focuses).

error.description: Names the scope that was not found.

KgValidationResponse.description: The result of validating cypher against the schema without executing it.

message.description: A single human-readable summary, or null when there is nothing to say.

ok.description: True when the cypher passes the strict preflight — the same check strict execution applies.

violations.description: What the schema contradicts, one entry per defect.

KgValueOverflow.description: A property's value domain that is wider than its declared `max`: how wide, and a sample of its shape.

count.description: How many distinct values exist. Null when the source could not be counted.

max.description: The cap that was exceeded — the property's declared `max`.

sample.description: A few values, to show the SHAPE of the domain. NEVER treat this as the set.

KgViewInvocationResponse.description: The runnable cypher for a saved view invoked with the given arguments.

cypher.description: Run this through `/execute`, so a view uses the same engine as any other query.

name.description: The view's name, as given in the path.

KgViewMatch.description: The saved view a question was routed to instead of generating Cypher.

args.description: The arguments the selector bound from the question, by parameter name.

name.description: The saved view's name, as `GET /views` lists it.

reason.description: The selector's one line on why this view.

url.description: The spec URL — an OpenAPI document or a GraphQL endpoint

LearnRequest.description: How to learn a source, sent to POST /learn/sources/{name}/learn. The body is optional: absent learns a realm under metadata consent with no purpose

consent.description: What learning may read: `metadata`, `distinct_values` or `sample_rows`, in any case. Absent or unrecognised means metadata. With descriptionsOnly only metadata and sample_rows apply; distinct_values is refused 400

descriptionsOnly.description: True drafts only a description of a connected ClickHouse database and answers a description proposal rather than a realm proposal; false (the default) learns a realm

purpose.description: One line about what the source is, given to the curator alongside the metadata; absent when none

LearningError.description: A refusal carrying only its explanation, with no code to branch on

error.description: What went wrong, written to be shown. Carries the underlying driver's or parser's own message where there is one

LearningRefused.description: A refusal that names a machine-readable code beside its explanation

code.description: The refusal's code, for a client that branches rather than reads. Every value comes from the sealed LearningReviewRefusal hierarchy, except SOURCE_UNREADABLE which the 502 path builds directly.

error.description: What was refused and what to do about it, written to be shown to the person reviewing

LensChatRequest.description: A question to answer grounded in a lens's focused entities; sent to POST /lenses/chat. The lens comes from lensId, else script, else is generated from english.

conversationId.description: Conversation to continue. Omit or leave blank on the first turn and the server starts one, answering its id as conversationId; pass that back on later turns.

english.description: Plain-English description the server generates a CypherScript lens from; used only when neither lensId nor script gives the lens

lensId.description: Id of a saved or world lens to open, e.g. briefing. When it is blank or names no lens, the lens is taken from script or english instead.

question.description: The question, answered by the main chat with the lens's focused entities added to the caller's working state

script.description: Ready CypherScript program to open as the lens; used when lensId gives none, and preferred over english

LensParam.description: A parameter a lens declares: the declaration only, so a UI can render a control for it. The value itself is passed in the args map when the lens is opened, keyed by name

default.description: Value used when the opener supplies none; null when there is no default

label.description: Text a UI shows for the control. Defaults to name when absent

name.description: Key the value is passed under in the args map when the lens is opened

required.description: Whether opening the lens fails when neither the opener nor default gives a value. Defaults to false when absent

type.description: Advisory type that picks the UI control and drives light validation. Defaults to STRING when absent

LensRefusal.description: A refusal from the lens authoring surface. Carries only the reason

error.description: Why the request was refused, written to be shown. Names the lens or view where the refusal is about one

LicenceSummary.description: The appliance's trial or licence as a client sees it: from GET /admin/licence, a successful key install, and the bootstrap response

daysLeft.description: Whole days until endsAt, rounded up; null when endsAt is null

endsAt.description: ISO-8601 instant at which the current state stops holding: the trial's end, or the key's expiry. Null under a key that never expires, and once expired

keyExpired.description: True when the appliance is expired because a licence key ran out, rather than the trial

licensee.description: Who the key in force was issued to (its name, else its email). Null outside `licensed`, or when the key names neither

registerUrl.description: Where to register for, or renew, a licence key

state.description: `trial`, `licensed` or `expired`. An expired appliance is locked until a valid key is entered

warn.description: True inside the warning window before endsAt: time to show a banner

LlmConfig.description: How one purpose, or one role override, picks its model: by role or by pinned model, with optional temperature and reasoning effort. Read and written by the /config/llms, /config/chat and /config/llm-roles endpoints

description.description: What a custom role in llmRoles is for, since built-in roles are described by the catalogue; unused on a purpose setting

model.description: Model name to pin. For a purpose, used only when no role is set; in an llmRoles entry, the model the role resolves to. Null or blank pins nothing

reasoningEffort.description: Reasoning effort: none, minimal, low, medium, high or xhigh (none turns a thinking model's reasoning off); null leaves the provider's default

role.description: Role id to select the model by (e.g. chat_best, code_best); for a purpose it takes precedence over model. Not used in an llmRoles entry

temperature.description: Sampling temperature; null keeps the default's temperature

LlmPurposeUpdated.description: One purpose's model settings as saved

model.description: The pinned model, or null when the purpose inherits one

purpose.description: The purpose that was changed, as named in the path

reasoningEffort.description: The reasoning effort the purpose runs at, or null for the model's default

temperature.description: The sampling temperature, or null for the model's default

LlmRoleUpdated.description: A role override as saved, or cleared

model.description: The model the request named, or null when it named none

roleId.description: The role that was changed, as named in the path

status.description: Always `updated`, including when the override was cleared

LlmSettings.description: The model settings one purpose runs with. Each field is null where this world sets nothing and the deployment default applies

model.description: The pinned model, or null when the purpose inherits one

reasoningEffort.description: The reasoning effort every call for this purpose runs at, or null for the model's default

temperature.description: The sampling temperature, or null for the model's default

LoadedSampleSet.description: One loaded sample set, and how much of this world it accounts for

name.description: The set's name, which is what removes it again

nodes.description: How many nodes this set put into the world

realm.description: The realm the set belongs to, where it came from one. Null for a set loaded on its own

LogEntry.description: One event this appliance process logged, as a structured line

logger.description: Simple name of the logger, package stripped — normally the logging class

message.description: The formatted message, with the first-run setup token redacted. No stack trace

thread.description: Name of the thread that logged it

timestamp.description: When the event was logged, in epoch milliseconds (UTC)

LogTail.description: What `GET /admin/logs` answers: the most recent events this process holds in memory. Not a container log, and lost on restart

bufferSize.description: How many events the in-memory buffer holds at most (200); asking for more cannot return more

entries.description: The entries, oldest first, after the `level` filter

truncated.description: True when as many entries came back as `limit` asked for, so older ones may have been cut off

McpDoorsView.description: Where a coding agent connects. The chat door is always there; the code door is present only on an appliance that enabled it, and its key is ABSENT rather than null when it is not.

chatAliasUrl.description: The same door under its alias, for a client pinned to the older path

developerUrl.description: The code door's URL, present only where the code door is enabled. ABSENT, not null, so `if (developerUrl)` is right on every server that ever shipped

url.description: The chat door's URL — a server fact no client can derive, because the published port is a host-side mapping

McpModeRequest.description: The mode a connected coding agent runs under

McpModeUpdated.description: The coding-agent mode was changed, and is live immediately

requiresReconnect.description: Always false: the gate is read on every call, so an already-connected client simply retries

McpModeView.description: What a connected coding agent may do, and what it could be set to

mode.description: The mode in force for this user, resolved through the service rather than re-derived from config

modes.description: Every mode this appliance offers, so a client need not hardcode the list

requiresReconnect.description: Always false. Nothing here needs a reconnect — the gate is read on every call, orientation re-reads the mode, and the realm tools export unconditionally. Kept as a field because clients already read it, and a client that stops telling people to reconnect is the point

McpServerInfo.description: An MCP server reachable from this world, configured by the world itself or wired in at the installation level

description.description: What the server is for, when its configuration says

name.description: The server's name, as its configuration gives it

toolCount.description: How many tools the server exposes. 0 for a world server not yet started, whose tools are discovered on first use

toolNames.description: The names of those tools; empty while the server has not been started

MemoryStatus.description: The JVM heap and the container it runs in

containerLimitBytes.description: The container's memory limit from cgroup v2. Null when unlimited or unreadable.

containerUsedBytes.description: Memory the container uses now, from cgroup v2. Null when unreadable.

heapAfterGcBytes.description: Heap in use straight after the most recent garbage collection — the closest cheap reading of what the app actually holds. Null until the first collection.

heapMaxBytes.description: The heap ceiling (-Xmx, or MaxRAMPercentage of the container). Null if the JVM sets none.

heapUsedBytes.description: Heap in use now, garbage included; rises and falls between collections

Message.description: The agent's answer in a chat completion

content.description: The agent's whole answer. When the turn raised requests still waiting for approval, it ends with a note listing each one, the run that raised it, and a link to decide it.

MintRequest.description: What to mint, the body of POST /api-keys

agents.description: Absent or null mints a full key. A list mints an agent key that may talk only to these agents (`*` for any) and reaches nothing else; blank entries are dropped, and at least one must remain

name.description: A label to recognise the key by. Required: 1 to 64 characters after trimming

MixedLabel.description: A label holding sample and real records at once — the case where a view over it returns both with nothing on the row to tell them apart

label.description: The label carrying both kinds

sample.description: How many of its nodes are sample data

Model.description: An agent, presented as an OpenAI model

created.description: When the list was made, in Unix epoch seconds; not when the agent was created

id.description: The agent's name; send it as model to talk to it

ModelCatalog.description: The language models the provider offers, and the one auto-selection picks

default.description: The model auto-selection picks; the first listed when none resolves, and empty when there are none

models.description: The model names. Empty when the provider could not be queried

modelsWithProvider.description: Each model with the provider that serves it. Absent, not empty, when the provider could not be queried

ModelInUse.description: One surface of the appliance (chat, documents, embeddings) and the model that serves it, as GET /models/in-use resolves it

local.description: True when the provider is one that runs on this machine (LM Studio, Ollama, Docker); false otherwise, including when the provider is unknown

model.description: Model name serving this surface, resolved the way the surface itself resolves it; null when none could be resolved

provider.description: Provider of the model, as the framework's model list names it (e.g. "LM Studio", "OpenAI"); null when there is no model or it is not in that list

purpose.description: What the model is used for, in the user's terms, as "<surface> — <explanation>": currently "Chat — what you talk to", "Documents — answering from your files" or "Embeddings — indexing and search"

ModelList.description: The agents the caller can talk to now, as OpenAI models; answered by GET /openai/v1/models and, holding just that agent, GET /agents/{name}/v1/models

data.description: Agents that may be talked to now and that the caller's API key, if scoped to some agents, reaches

ModelRunnerActivity.description: Docker Model Runner's embedding model, as its own process list reports it

busy.description: Whether that model is serving a request now. It runs on the host, outside the app's container, so its CPU is not in the cpu figures.

loaded.description: Whether an embedding model is loaded. Model Runner loads one on the first request and unloads it when idle.

ModelWithProvider.description: One model and the provider that serves it

name.description: The model's name

NewDuty.description: A duty an add-duty change would give the agent

every.description: Six-field cron the duty is checked on; null means checked on demand

holds.description: The view or DERIVE label whose rows are the duty's violations

name.description: Name of the new duty; must not match one the agent already has

text.description: The duty's Always/Never rule, in words

NewRoleRequest.description: Body of POST /config/router/roles: a custom role of this world's own, which a context can then use

description.description: What the role is for

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter

NextStepList.description: Every declared onboarding step, done ones included. Which to show and in what order is the client's decision

NextStepState.description: One onboarding step and the answer to its own question

detail.description: Why the status is UNKNOWN, in the step author's words; null otherwise

dismissed.description: The user said they will not do this step. Orthogonal to status: a dismissed step that gets done still reports DONE

id.description: The step's id, as the dismiss endpoint names it

presentation.description: Everything else the step's YAML declared, carried through uninterpreted: a console reads a route from it, a chat surface an input. Open by contract

status.description: DONE, TODO, or UNKNOWN when the step's query could not be answered — which must not be shown as outstanding work

NodeRequest.description: One node of a sample set, as loaded by POST /samples and returned by POST /samples/export

displayName.description: Name the node is shown by; null leaves any name it already has. Null in a shape-only export

id.description: Identity of the node within its label in this world; loading merges on it, so loading a set again updates rather than duplicates. Edges name nodes by it. A shape-only export replaces it with `n1`, `n2`, ...

label.description: The node's label: a letter, then up to 63 letters, digits or underscores

properties.description: Further property values set on the node, by key; a key starting with `_` is refused. A shape-only export keeps the keys and blanks the values: text becomes `…`, numbers 0, lists item by item, booleans are kept

Notification.description: A notification to raise for the authenticated user, the body of POST /notifications. A simple alert sets event, source and url; the consequence engine fills the richer fields

actionKind.description: The kind of action recommended, which chooses the Act button and the handler it calls. Null when there is nothing to act on

confidence.description: How sure the producer is that this matters, from 0 to 1. Null when the producer did not say

consequenceOfInaction.description: One sentence on what happens if the user does nothing. Null on simple alerts

createdAt.description: When the notification was generated, an ISO-8601 instant. Defaults to the moment the server read the body

createdBy.description: Who produced it, such as engine.v1 or github-action. "user" claims the user asked for it; anything else goes through the admission filter. Defaults to "system"

deadline.description: When this stops being actionable, an ISO-8601 instant. Null when there is no hard deadline

event.description: One-sentence headline saying what happened; the card's title

id.description: Stable id, which the read and dismiss endpoints take in their path

kind.description: How it relates to earlier notifications on the same signals. The server sets UPDATE when it supersedes one, whatever the body said

read.description: Whether the user has marked it read

recommendation.description: One sentence giving the recommended next step. Null on simple alerts

source.description: What produced it, such as github, build, email or calendar. Free text. A new notification with the same source and headline as an unread one replaces it

sourceSignalIds.description: Ids of the persisted signals it was derived from. A later notification sharing any of them supersedes this one

sources.description: Backlinks to each signal or system the notification cites. Empty on simple alerts

supersedes.description: Ids of the earlier notifications this one replaced, which were dismissed when it was published. The ids may no longer resolve

tier.description: Urgency tier, which sets styling and the surfaces it is delivered to. The admission filter may lower it. Defaults to AMBIENT

url.description: Link the user can open to act in the originating system. Null when there is none

userId.description: The user the notification belongs to. Ignored on create: the server sets it to the authenticated user

whyItMatters.description: One sentence on why the user should care. Null on simple alerts

NotificationAck.description: Confirmation that one notification changed state

id.description: The notification this acknowledges, echoed from the path

status.description: What the notification now is: `read` or `dismissed`

NotificationBulkAck.description: Confirmation that every notification changed state at once

status.description: What they all now are: `all_read` or `all_dismissed`. No id, because the call named none

NotificationNode.description: A stored notification as the /notifications endpoints answer it. List-valued fields arrive as JSON-encoded strings

actionKind.description: Name of the recommended action kind, such as DRAFT_REPLY or ACK_ONLY. Null when there is nothing to act on

confidence.description: How sure the producer was that this matters, from 0 to 1. Null when it did not say

consequenceOfInaction.description: One sentence on what happens if the user does nothing. Null on simple alerts

created.description: When the notification was generated, an ISO-8601 instant

createdBy.description: Who produced it: "user" when the user asked for it, otherwise the producer's id, such as "system" or engine.v1

deadline.description: When this stops being actionable, an ISO-8601 instant. Null when there is no hard deadline

id.description: Stable id, which the read and dismiss endpoints take in their path

kind.description: How it relates to earlier notifications on the same signals: ORIGINAL, UPDATE, CANCELLATION or COMPLETION

read.description: Whether the user has marked it read

recommendation.description: One sentence giving the recommended next step. Null on simple alerts

source.description: What produced it, such as github, build, email or calendar

sourceSignalIdsJson.description: The ids of the signals it was derived from, as a JSON-encoded array of strings

sourcesJson.description: The cited sources as a JSON-encoded array of {kind, id, displayLabel, url, typeName} objects; "[]" when there are none

supersedesJson.description: Ids of the earlier notifications it replaced, as a JSON-encoded array of strings

tier.description: Urgency tier name: AMBIENT, DEFERRED, TIMELY, INTERRUPTIVE, ACTING or ESCALATING

url.description: Link to act on it in the originating system. Null when there is none

userId.description: The user the notification belongs to; always the caller

whyItMatters.description: One sentence on why the user should care. Null on simple alerts

NotificationRoutingConfig.description: The user's notification routing: which channels each urgency tier reaches, and their quiet hours. Stored in the world config; read by GET /config/notification-routing and part of GET /config

quietHours.description: The user's quiet-hours window, replacing the deployment one; null inherits the deployment window

tierChannels.description: Urgency tier name (AMBIENT, DEFERRED, TIMELY, INTERRUPTIVE, ACTING, ESCALATING) to the channel kinds it reaches, such as vaadin, telegram, discord or sms. A tier present here replaces the deployment default for that tier; an absent tier inherits it

quietHours.description: The quiet-hours window, as stored. Null where this world sets none

tierChannels.description: Which channels each tier routes to, as stored — a tier may fan out to several

NotificationSource.description: A backlink from a notification to one signal or system it cites, kept on the notification so it still reads after the signal is gone

displayLabel.description: Short text shown for this source on the notification's Sources line

id.description: The source's own id within that system, such as an email thread id or a calendar event id

kind.description: What kind of system the source is, such as email, calendar or github. Free text, used to group sources in the UI

typeName.description: The domain type name of the signal this source came from. With id, it keys the signal's handling record, which publishing marks as notified. Empty when not set

url.description: Link to the item in the originating system. Null when not known

OAuth2AccountDisconnected.description: One account of an OAuth2 provider was disconnected

accountId.description: The account disconnected, as the path named it

provider.description: The provider the account belonged to

OAuth2ClientNotConfigured.description: The provider is declared, but no OAuth2 client app is configured for it, so there is no consent screen to send the caller to

error.description: Why, naming the provider

remedy.description: What an operator does to make the provider connectable

OAuth2ProviderDisconnected.description: Every account of one OAuth2 provider was disconnected

removed.description: How many registered accounts were removed. The provider's default slot is cleared as well and is not counted

OAuth2ProviderNotFound.description: The OAuth2 provider named in the path is not one this world declares with OAuth2 auth

error.description: Why, naming the provider asked for

OfferedChannel.description: One audience channel this world's content declares, and how much content joining it would reach.

apps.description: Number of apps in this world that declare the channel

channel.description: Channel name, normalised to trimmed lowercase

views.description: Number of saved views in this world that declare the channel

OnboardingRequest.description: Body of POST /onboarding/run: which sources to profile, how far back, and whether to build a Me app as well

buildMeApp.description: Also build a personal Me app (me.html) from the persona once it is saved, which is the expensive step. Defaults to false

lookbackDays.description: How many days of past activity to profile. Defaults to 30

sources.description: Source ids to profile, as GET /onboarding/sources lists them (`email`, `calendar`, `osx`). An empty list profiles every source that is available

OnboardingSource.description: A source the Get-to-Know-Me flow can profile, and whether it can be used now

available.description: Whether the source can be profiled now. False when no contributor for it is currently available on this server

id.description: Stable source id to send in an onboarding request: `email`, `calendar` or `osx`

label.description: Human-readable name to show for the source

OnboardingStartResponse.description: The 202 answer to POST /onboarding/run: the job started in the background. Poll GET /onboarding/status/{jobId} for its outcome

jobId.description: Id of the started job (a UUID), for GET /onboarding/status/{jobId}

PostMessageRequest.description: A message to post in a thread; sent to POST /threads/{id}/messages. At least one of text and attachments must be non-empty

attachments.description: Records, views or requests to attach, resolved and frozen when the message is posted; one that cannot be resolved is dropped, and at most 10 are kept

text.description: The message text. Every agent it @mentions answers in the thread in the background; with no mention at all, the agent who spoke last in the thread answers

PreferencesBody.description: Preferences to store, the body of PUT /profile/preferences. Both flags are always written, so an absent one takes its default

boltMode.description: `virtual` or `persisted`, in any case: the surface a Bolt connection gets when it names no database. Absent leaves the choice as it is; blank clears it back to the port's default

greetingEnabled.description: Greet the user when they sign in. Absent means false

hintsEnabled.description: Show the login hints popup. Absent means true

PreferencesView.description: The user's sign-in preferences and Bolt default, answered by GET and PUT /profile/preferences

boltMode.description: The surface a Bolt connection gets when it names no database: `virtual` (Virtual Cypher, read-only) or `persisted` (the stored graph, read and write). Null for the Bolt port's own default

greetingEnabled.description: Whether the assistant greets the user when they sign in

hintsEnabled.description: Whether the login hints popup shows

Principles.description: The appliance's effective architectural principles, as coding agents receive them, and where they came from; answered by GET /admin/principles

content.description: The principles text, plain text or markdown, exactly as coding agents receive it; empty only if the shipped default is missing

overridden.description: True when the operator's own file is in force; false when the shipped default is

PrinciplesRefusal.description: A refused write of the operator's principles

message.description: Why the write was refused, written to be shown

PrinciplesReset.description: The outcome of dropping the operator's principles: the shipped default is in force afterwards either way

overridden.description: Whether an operator override is in force after the reset. Always false

removed.description: True when an operator file existed and was removed, false when the default was already in force

status.description: Always ok: a reset cannot be refused

ProfileView.description: The signed-in user's display name and home location, answered by GET /profile and by the profile writes

displayName.description: The name the assistant uses for this user. Never null: until a name is set it falls back to the account's id

home.description: Home location, or null when none is set

PromoteRequest.description: The name to promote a reviewed provisional realm to, sent to POST /learn/{id}/promote

name.description: The promoted realm's directory name in this world; a realm of that name already existing is refused 409, since promotion never overwrites

ProposalResponse.description: A learning proposal to review before anything is written: what was read, what was decided and asked, the realm it would install, and where it stands. Answered by the learn, proposal, answer, approval and change endpoints; every part is flattened into one object

id.description: The proposal's id, for the /learn/{id} endpoints. Held in memory for its owner only; another user's or an expired one answers 404

source.description: Name of the source it was learned from, as SourceWire.name gives it

summary.description: One line to show when the pass finishes: tables, decisions, joins that returned rows, open questions and decisions applied unconfirmed

QosSpec.description: An agent's quality of service: the priority its work is paced at, and the models it falls back to when one of its own fails mid-check

fallbacks.description: Fallback model names keyed by LLM role. A check whose models and fallbacks all fail is held as unknown, never as upheld

priority.description: interactive, business (the default) or background. Background work takes half of each source it declares no share for; a conversation is interactive whatever is declared

QuietHoursConfig.description: A daily quiet-hours window in the user's local time, during which push channels are vetoed for every tier except ESCALATING

enabled.description: Whether the window is applied; false means no quiet hours for this user, even when the deployment has them

end.description: End of the window, HH:mm local time, inclusive

start.description: Start of the window, HH:mm local time; a window whose start is after its end runs past midnight

RealmDirectoryBrowse.description: Every realm the directory knows, grouped by the account or organisation that publishes it

complete.description: False when a source scan failed or returned partial results, so some realms may be missing

RealmDirectoryListing.description: One installable realm as the browse lists it

description.description: What the realm is for, as its publisher describes it

installed.description: True when a realm of this name is already loaded in the caller's world

metadata.description: The source's own extras for this realm, passed through as reported. Open by contract

name.description: The realm's name, as an install names it

source.description: Where the realm installs from: a git clone URL or registry identifier

url.description: A human-readable page for the realm, or null when the source has none

provider.description: The publishing account or organisation, from the entry's `from` metadata, or "unknown"

RealmDirectoryUnavailable.description: The realm scan is incomplete and found nothing, so there is no partial catalogue to show

message.description: What to do about it, written to be shown

RealmGaps.description: What this world could add: realms it could install, APIs that are inert and what would unlock each, and structural gaps

inertApis.description: APIs declared but inert, with the reason and what would make each answer

structuralGaps.description: Gaps in the world's shape, each written as a sentence

RealmLogEntry.description: One log line a realm's guest code wrote during a dispatch

dispatchId.description: Id of the dispatch the line was logged in, which groups the lines of one handler run. Null when not recorded

level.description: The log level: TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR

message.description: The log message as written, except that a first-run setup token in it is redacted

realm.description: The realm that logged it. Null when the code path never recorded which realm it was running for

timestamp.description: When the line was logged, in epoch milliseconds

RealmLogTail.description: The newest guest log lines from the process-wide log ring buffer, answered by GET /admin/realms/observability/logs

bufferSize.description: How many events the ring buffer holds across the whole process, so no request can return more than this

captureEnabled.description: False when this deployment captures no log lines at all, because diagnostics are off; entries is then empty whatever the realms did

entries.description: The matching lines, oldest first and newest last, at most the requested limit

filteredOut.description: True when a realm was named, nothing matched it, and the buffer did hold other guest lines

RealmNeedsConfirmation.description: Not a failure: the realm is experimental and asks the owner to confirm. Retrying with `confirmed: true` installs it

message.description: What the realm says the owner is confirming

name.description: The realm that asked

RealmProblemResponse.description: One problem found with a realm, with its cause, a suggested fix, and where it is when known.

column.description: 1-based column in the file, when known

file.description: The file, relative to the realm root, when known

line.description: 1-based line in the file, when known

message.description: What went wrong

path.description: The YAML path inside the file, when known

severity.description: NOTE is worth a look and leaves the realm active; WARNING degrades a feature; ERROR breaks one

source.description: Where the problem was found, such as `realms/<name>` or `realms/<name>/producers/x.yml`

suggestion.description: How to fix it, when there is a suggestion

RealmRefusal.description: A refusal from the realms surface: the word `error` and the reason

message.description: Why the request was refused, written to be shown. A failed install or update carries the underlying failure's message

admission.description: What happened to the realm's approval

data.description: What became of the nodes the realm seeded and the documents it ingested, counted per type and per source. Absent when removal touched no data

name.description: The realm removed

RealmRuntimeSnapshot.description: Point-in-time read of the realm runtime and JVM meters, answered by GET /admin/realms/observability/metrics. Counts and totals are cumulative since the process started.

jvm.description: JVM memory, thread, garbage-collection and CPU readings

RealmUpdateResult.description: What updating one realm did. A failed row carries `message` in place of `summary`

message.description: Why the pull failed. Present only on a failure

name.description: The realm's name

status.description: `updated` after a pull, `local` for a realm loaded in place, `error` when the pull failed

summary.description: What the pull did, or that a local realm is loaded in place. Absent on a failure

RealmUpdateResults.description: The outcome of updating every realm, one row each. One realm failing does not stop the rest

RealmUpdateState.description: Whether one realm has a newer version upstream. A legacy per-world clone answers only `name`, `behind` and `detail`

behind.description: True when there is something to pull, false when current, null when it cannot be told — including while the first read is still running

checkedAt.description: When the remote was read, ISO-8601. Absent for a legacy clone, null when not yet read

current.description: The local checkout's revision. Absent for a legacy clone

detail.description: Why the answer is what it is, in words a user can act on. Always present, including for the unknowns

latest.description: The remote's revision. Absent for a legacy clone

name.description: The realm's name

RealmUpdateStates.description: Per installed realm, whether its upstream has moved

RealmsRefreshed.description: The world was rebuilt, and these realms are loaded now

realms.description: The names of the realms loaded after the rebuild

Receipt.description: One decision the Gatekeeper made about a call that would change something on a run's behalf (acted, held for a person, or refused), or a person's answer to such a request. Chained per owner by hash so an edit shows; returned with its run by GET /agents/{name}/runs/{id}

agent.description: Name of the agent holding the work; null when no agent holds it

agentVersion.description: The holding agent's governing signed version number when the decision was made; null when none governs it

at.description: ISO-8601 instant it was written, to the millisecond

decidedBy.description: Username of the person who approved or rejected; null when the Gatekeeper decided

decision.description: `act` (let through), `request` (held for a person), `refused`, or a person's `approved` or `rejected`

entityKeys.description: Business records the call's arguments name, as `field=value`: a field called `id`, `key`, `number`, `res_id` or `external_id`, or ending `Id`, `_id`, `Key`, `_key`, `Url` or `_url`. At most 20

hash.description: SHA-256 hex over everything else this receipt says, as canonical JSON with keys sorted and times as ISO-8601 text

id.description: The receipt's id, `rc_` and a UUID

inputHash.description: SHA-256 hex of the call's input as sent, or of the empty string when it had none

ownerId.description: Id of the user whose chain the receipt belongs to

previousHash.description: The hash of the receipt before it in the owner's chain; empty for the first

reason.description: Why, in words, up to 500 characters; empty when none was given

requestId.description: Id of the request it raised or answered; null for `act` and `refused`

rule.description: What decided: `authority`, `halted`, `egress`, `observing`, `never` or `review` for the Gatekeeper, `person` for a person's answer; `refused` when a refusal named no rule

runId.description: Id of the run the decision was made for; null for a person's answer to a request that names no run

seq.description: Position in the owner's chain, counting from 1

verb.description: The verb called, as the gateway names it

work.description: Name of the routine the call was made from

RememberFactRequest.description: One already-formed fact to store verbatim in the caller's memory as an ACTIVE proposition, by POST /memory/remember

confidence.description: How sure the fact is, from 0 to 1, a value outside clamped to that range; absent or null means 0.9. Unused when the fact matches an existing one

text.description: The statement to remember, trimmed; must not be blank, and at most 2,000 characters. When an ACTIVE proposition in the caller's current context already has this text, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace, that one is returned and nothing is stored

RememberRefusal.description: A refused fact. Carries only the reason

error.description: Why the fact was refused: blank, or longer than the limit

RememberedFact.description: The fact as remembered: the proposition just stored, or the existing one whose text it matched

id.description: The proposition's id

text.description: The proposition's text. For a duplicate, the EXISTING text, which may differ from the request in case and surrounding whitespace

RequestMessage.description: One message of an OpenAI chat request's history

content.description: A string, or a list of content parts of which only the {type: text, text} ones are read, joined by newlines; anything else reads as empty

role.description: user or assistant; messages with any other role, such as system, are not read

ResolvedModel.description: A model as the router resolves it: its name, who serves it, and whether it runs on this machine

local.description: True when its provider runs locally: LM Studio, Ollama or Docker

name.description: The model's name, as the appliance's model provider knows it

provider.description: Who serves it, as the model provider names it (for example `LM Studio`); null when the model is not among those the provider lists

RetireRequest.description: Why an agent is being retired, sent to POST /agents/{name}/retire

reason.description: The reason, recorded with the retirement after trimming; may be empty

Retired.description: What retiring an agent took with it, as POST /agents/{name}/retire answers: the agent is off duty for good and its record is kept

agent.description: Name of the agent that was retired

keysRevoked.description: How many of your API keys were revoked because they could talk to this agent, including keys scoped to other agents as well

slotsDeleted.description: How many of the agent's own credential slots (its own-account secrets) were deleted from your wallet

RoleModelRequest.description: Body of PUT /config/router/roles/{id}: the model a role uses in this world

model.description: The model the role uses in this world; blank for the deployment's choice

RoleView.description: One LLM role, standard, mapped by the deployment, or added by this world, with the model it resolves to and the contexts that use it. Part of GET /config/router

custom.description: True for a role this world added, the only kind that can be deleted

deploymentModel.description: The model the deployment maps this role to in `embabel.models.llms`; null when it maps none

description.description: What the role is for; null for a role only the deployment declares, which carries no description

group.description: Where a standard role is shown: `GENERAL` or `VIRTUAL_CYPHER`; null for deployment and custom roles

id.description: The role's id, such as `chat_best` or `vc_execution`

resolved.description: The model the role reaches now: this world's choice when it made one, else what the platform selects for the role; null when nothing can serve it

usedBy.description: Ids of the contexts that reach their model through this role

worldModel.description: The model this world chose for the role, overriding the deployment's; null when it chose none

RouterChangeApplied.description: The change was applied and the world's config saved; it takes effect on the next request

ok.description: Always true. A client that only branches on the status code can ignore it; one that reads the body does not have to special-case the shape

RouterChangeRefused.description: The change was refused and nothing was saved. The status code says which kind of refusal: 400 for something unknown or invalid, 409 while a context still uses the role

detail.description: Why it was refused, written to be shown. Carries the router's own sentence, which names the context, role or model at fault

RouterView.description: The whole model-routing chain of the signed-in user's world, resolved: contexts, roles, the models available, and the deployment's own model settings. Answered by GET /config/router

contexts.description: Every context, with the role or model it uses and the model that resolves

deploymentUses.description: Model settings the deployment makes that no world can change yet

models.description: The language models the appliance can serve, local ones first, then by name

roles.description: Standard roles first, then the deployment's, then this world's custom roles

RoutineRef.description: A routine an agent holds: a TypeScript action, by name, that fires on a schedule or a signal

action.description: Name of the action in the world's actions

stage.description: Stage for this routine alone (off, observing or on); null runs it as the agent. Dropped from a realm-shipped agent

RoutineView.description: A routine on an agent's card (AgentView.routines): a TypeScript action or realm-scheduled function, with the stage chosen for it and the stage it actually fires at

description.description: The action's own description; empty when the routine does not exist in this world

firing.description: The stage dispatch actually honours for it (off, observing or on). Lower than `stage` when something the agent still needs holds it back; off for a missing routine

missing.description: True when the agent names a routine that does not exist in this world

name.description: The action's name, as the agent names it

stage.description: The stage chosen for this routine (off, observing or on): a stored override, else its declared stage, else the agent's, before the agent's own standing is applied

trigger.description: What fires it, in words: "when <signal type> arrives", "on schedule <cron>", "on the realm's schedule <cron>", both joined by a comma, "no trigger", or "not found" for a missing routine

RunDetail.description: One run of an agent, with a receipt for every decision made on its behalf; answered by GET /agents/{name}/runs/{id}

receipts.description: Receipts for the decisions the Gatekeeper made during the run, in the order they were made

run.description: The run itself: what started it, its state, timing and output

RunNowRequest.description: One of an agent's scheduled jobs to run now, outside its schedule; sent to POST /agents/{name}/upcoming/run

job.description: Name of the scheduled job, as a firing's job in GET /agents/{name}/upcoming

RunSavedRequest.description: Optional body for opening a saved lens — POST /lenses/{id}/run, /present, /views and /views/{view} — carrying values for its declared parameters

args.description: Parameter values keyed by parameter name. They override the declared defaults; a required parameter with neither a value nor a default fails the open. Empty or absent uses the defaults.

idempotencyKey.description: The caller's key for this request; a repeat with the same key for the same watch returns the original run instead of running again. Omitted or blank, every call runs

SampleDataCleared.description: Every sample node removed, whatever loaded it

nodes.description: How many nodes went. Zero means this world held no sample data

SampleDataExportResponse.description: Answer of POST /samples/export: the selected records as a sample set in the body POST /samples accepts, and whether the limit cut it short

edges.description: Relationships between exported nodes only, named by the ids used in nodes

matched.description: How many records the selection found before the limit was applied

name.description: Name of the exported set, as the request gave it

nodes.description: The exported records in id order, at most the request's limit, each under its first label other than the internal ones

realm.description: Realm name recorded on the set, as the request gave it

truncated.description: True when the selection found more records than nodes holds

SampleLoadResult.description: What a sample-data load did, or why it refused. The same shape either way: a refusal is this with `ok` false and the reasons in `problems`

edges.description: How many edges were written. Zero on a refusal

nodes.description: How many nodes were written. Zero on a refusal

ok.description: Whether the set was loaded. False means nothing was written and `problems` says why

problems.description: Why the load was refused, one sentence per problem. Empty when `ok` is true

SampleSetRemoved.description: One sample set removed, and how much went with it

nodes.description: How many nodes that set had loaded. Zero means the name matched nothing

removed.description: The set that was removed, echoed back unchanged

SampleSetRequest.description: Body of POST /samples: a named set of fictional records for one realm. Its nodes are marked `:_Sample` and tagged with the set's name, so the set can be removed without touching real records. POST /samples/export answers this same shape.

edges.description: Relationships to create, each with at least one end among this set's nodes; empty when omitted

matched.description: Accepted so an export loads back as written, and ignored

name.description: Name of the set, tagged on every node it loads; DELETE /samples/{name} removes it. Must not be blank

nodes.description: The records to load, at least one; ids must be unique within the set

realm.description: Name of the realm whose types the set populates. Must not be blank

truncated.description: Accepted so an export loads back as written, and ignored

SampleSetsLoaded.description: What sample data this world holds: the sets that were loaded, and any label where sample records now sit beside real ones

mixedLabels.description: Labels holding sample and real records at once. Reported alongside deliberately: the answer to "what is loaded" is incomplete without "and is any of it sitting next to real records of the same type"

sets.description: One entry per loaded set, with how many nodes it put in

SamplingSpec.description: What a caller may set on a conversation with an agent: a temperature range, and the most tokens a reply may take. A value asked for is clamped into these bounds

maxTokens.description: The most tokens a caller may ask a reply to take; null declares no cap

temperature.description: Allowed temperature range as two numbers [low, high]; any other length is ignored. Null declares no range

query.description: The text to match against the user's memories

topK.description: How many results to return; clamped to 1..30

SecretValue.description: The agent's own value for a secret, sent to PUT /agents/{name}/accounts/{secret}

value.description: The secret value itself, kept as an API key and sent instead of the sponsor's on an own-account API; never returned

SectionChunkView.description: One chunk of a section's words, as it was cut from the document at ingest

id.description: The chunk's id in the document store

text.description: The chunk's text as cut, without the provenance lines added to it for embedding

SectionHeadingView.description: One heading of a stored document: where it sits in the document, and what it is called

depth.description: 1 for a heading directly inside the document, 2 for one inside that, and so on. Null when not recorded

hasText.description: Whether it has words of its own to read. A heading can have both words and headings inside it

id.description: The section's id: what `sectionId` on a `POST /documents/ask` source refers to

leaf.description: Whether it has no headings inside it

ordinal.description: Its place in reading order, counted from 0: the `ordinal` GET /documents/sections takes. Not every number is used. Null when the stored section carries none

parentId.description: Id of what this heading sits directly inside: the enclosing heading, or the document itself for a top-level heading. Null when not recorded

Sender.description: Who wrote a thread message: the person, one of their agents, or the appliance explaining why something did not happen

kind.description: PERSON for the thread's owner, AGENT for an agent, APPLIANCE for the appliance's own notices

name.description: The person's username, the agent's name, or appliance

SensorBatchRequest.description: A batch of events the sensor app on the user's machine pushes to POST /sensor/events

events.description: The events, each discriminated by its `kind` (`fact` or `context`). Each gets its own receipt

source.description: Which sensor is talking, e.g. `me-app`. Must not be blank; context streams are namespaced under it

timeZone.description: IANA zone of the sensor's machine, e.g. `Australia/Sydney`. A valid zone becomes the user's time zone; an invalid one is ignored, and absent leaves the user's zone as it is

SensorBatchResponse.description: What became of a sensor batch: counts by outcome, and a receipt per event

duplicates.description: Facts skipped because the same text, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace, is already an active memory in the user's current context

observed.description: Context events recorded as what the user is doing now

receipts.description: One receipt per event, in the order the events were sent. A blank-source 400 carries a single receipt instead

rejected.description: Events refused. On a blank-source 400 this is every event in the batch

SensorCommand.description: A command the appliance asks the user's machine to run, delivered by the GET /sensor/outbox long-poll

id.description: Command id (a UUID). The sensor posts the result to /sensor/outbox/{id}/result

kind.description: The verb to run: a name the sensor itself published in its capabilities catalog

payload.description: The verb's arguments, keyed by the argument names the sensor published for it

SessionSummaryResponse.description: One of the caller's persisted chat sessions, metadata only; listed by GET /chat/sessions

createdAt.description: When the session was created, as an ISO-8601 instant

heldWith.description: Username of the agent an agent's own session is held with; null for any other session

kind.description: How the session is talked to: CHAT through the chat stream, THREAD through /threads, AGENT by the client holding an agent's session, CHANNEL through Telegram, Slack or Discord

lastActivityAt.description: When the session last had activity, as an ISO-8601 instant; the list is sorted on it, newest first

sessionId.description: Session id; pass it as sessionId to GET /chat/stream to open the session, or to DELETE /chat/sessions/{sessionId}

startedBy.description: Who wrote the session's first message: the user, an agent, or the appliance; null while nobody has written in it

title.description: The session's title; null while it has none

SetContextBody.description: The context to switch to, the body of PUT /context/current

name.description: Context name, trimmed. Must not be blank; a name not used before starts a new, empty context

SetStageRequest.description: A move on the stage ladder for an agent, or for one routine it holds; sent to POST /agents/{name}/stage

routine.description: Name of one routine the agent holds, to move only that routine; null or absent moves the agent as a whole

stage.description: Stage to move to: off (never fires), observing (runs with writes suppressed) or on (may write). An unrecognised value reads as off

SignalBackfillRefusal.description: A backfill that was refused or failed. Carries only the reason

error.description: Why: an out-of-range lookback, or the failure the backfill reported

SignalBackfillReport.description: The outcome of replaying the trailing window from every time-window ingestion source

durationMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the backfill in milliseconds

results.description: One row per ingestion source, whether it ran or was skipped

since.description: The start of the replayed window, ISO-8601

username.description: The user the backfill ran for

SignalBackfillSourceResult.description: What one ingestion source did during a backfill

detail.description: Why a source was skipped or failed; null when there is nothing to add

fetched.description: How many signals the source returned, before dedup

published.description: How many of those were new and reached the bus. Re-running a backfill publishes only what was not seen before

status.description: Whether the source ran: a BackfillStatus name, such as Ok, Failed, or one of the Skipped reasons

SignalTypeInfo.description: One signal type this world has received, as GET /signal-types lists them busiest first: its fields, how many arrived in the window asked for, and when the last one did

count.description: How many signals of this type occurred within the last `days` days; 0 for a type seen in the field sample but not in that window

fields.description: Property keys this type carries, sorted, as seen on the 400 most recent signals of any type; empty when none of those was of this type

lastSeen.description: The latest occurredAt among those counted, as a date-time string; empty when none fell in the window

typeName.description: The signal's graph label, such as EmailReceivedSignal: the label ending in Signal other than Signal itself

SkillSummary.description: One skill installed in the caller's world, as the chat's model is offered it; listed by GET /skills. A connected SQL database that carries a description is listed alongside the skills

description.description: What the skill is for, as the model reads it when deciding whether to use it

name.description: Skill name, or for a connected SQL database its datasource name

SkipRequest.description: Skip the next scheduled firing of one of an agent's jobs, or postpone it; sent to POST /agents/{name}/upcoming/skip

job.description: Name of the scheduled job, as a firing's job in GET /agents/{name}/upcoming

reason.description: Why, kept with the skip after trimming; may be empty

until.description: When to run the skipped firing instead, ISO-8601 instant in the future; null or absent skips it outright

Slots.description: The secrets an agent keeps its own value for, by name only; answered by the /agents/{name}/accounts endpoints

secrets.description: Names of the secrets the agent has its own value for, as the realm's keys declare them, sorted; the values are never returned

Source.description: One document a `POST /documents/ask` retrieved, with the passages read from it.

cited.description: True on every source of a composed answer: each is a document the answering model was observed to retrieve. False when `answer` was false.

dates.description: The document's modified, created and ingested dates.

n.description: Citation number, from 1 in retrieval order: the `[n]` an answer cites this document by.

passages.description: Verbatim text of the chunks of this document that retrieval read, best first, each cut to `maxSnippet` characters, with the provenance lines added at ingest removed.

score.description: Relevance of the document's best-matching chunk, normally 0 to 1. Vector and full-text scores are not calibrated against each other, so `n` gives the order, not this.

sectionId.description: The heading the first passage sits under, by the id GET /documents/outline lists it with, so a reader can open the document there. Null when the passage does not say.

title.description: The document's title. `?` or null when the matched chunk did not record one.

uri.description: The document's uri, as GET /documents lists it. Empty or null when the matched chunk did not record it.

SourceDates.description: A source document's three dates, each an ISO-8601 instant, or null when the document has none.

createdAt.description: When the document itself was created, as an ISO-8601 instant. Null when unknown.

ingestedAt.description: When this appliance ingested the document, as an ISO-8601 instant. Null when unknown.

modifiedAt.description: When the document itself last changed, as an ISO-8601 instant. Null when unknown.

SourceLinkRefusal.description: A cited source that cannot be resolved to an external URL

error.description: Why: the kind has no resolver here, or the resolver does not know the id or will not show it to this caller

SourceWire.description: One source this appliance can reach, with the evidence that makes it worth learning and what has been learned from it so far

asserts.description: What a store of this kind asserts itself, e.g. foreign-key edges and column types for SQL

confirmation.description: How much a person must confirm before a realm learned from this kind is fit to query: LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH

connected.description: True when the user connected it, so it may be edited or disconnected; false for one a realm declares

evidence.description: The structured evidence behind summary, by name, for a client that renders more than a sentence

inferred.description: What learning has to infer for a store of this kind, beyond what it asserts

installedRealm.description: Directory name of the provisional realm installed from it (`auto-<source>`); null when none is installed

kind.description: What kind of store it is: GRAPHQL, SQL, OPENAPI, ELASTICSEARCH or TABULAR

label.description: The kind in words, e.g. `relational database`

learnable.description: False for kinds this appliance can detect but not yet learn

name.description: The handle the learning endpoints take as {name}: for SQL the registered datasource name, for an API its gateway namespace

neededBy.description: Loaded realms that name this source as a SQL datasource, sorted; every one of them stops answering if it is disconnected. Always empty for an API, which realms do not name this way

pendingReview.description: The id of the caller's latest review still held for it (GET /learn/{id}), so a client can resume without keeping the id; null when none is held

promotedRealms.description: Names of the realms promoted from it, sorted; empty when none

reachable.description: False when detection found the source but could not reach it

summary.description: One line to show verbatim: what was found, and what about it suggests it is worth learning

SourcesResponse.description: The sources this appliance can reach and could learn, answered by GET /learn/sources

sources.description: Every detected source, reachable or not, described from metadata alone

SqlAbout.description: The SQL door: the Postgres wire protocol, which psql, JDBC and BI tools connect to.

address.description: The address the server advertises for the door, host:port

answers.description: What that database answers, in a sentence

database.description: The database the door answers as, whatever name a client connects to

url.description: The URL to connect to; the client supplies the user and password

StageResponse.description: The agent after a stage change or signature, or why the change was refused; answered by POST /agents/{name}/stage and POST /agents/{name}/sign

agent.description: The agent after the change; null when it was refused

refused.description: Why the change was refused, in words; null when it was made

StartFillRequest.description: What to fill: the body of POST /admin/kg/fills

budgetPerTick.description: Units of paid work one tick may buy: a producer fetch group or a group of an inline model judgement, not HTTP requests or tokens. Clamped to 1-500; defaults to 60 when absent

cypher.description: The Virtual Cypher query whose materialization the fill drives; every tick re-runs it. Blank is a 400

label.description: Display name for the fill, shown in its activity; empty when absent, and the fill id is shown instead

StorageEngineInfo.description: Which graph engine this appliance stores its memory in

engine.description: The engine's name, as the deployment configured it

SuggestionResponse.description: A suggested colleague after it was recorded, drafted, adopted or dismissed, or why that was refused; answered by the /agent-suggestions endpoints

refused.description: Why the change was refused, in words; null when it was made

suggestion.description: The suggestion after the change; null when it was refused

SurfaceDictionary.description: What a connected surface says it can be told to do: its tour dictionary, sent to POST /ui/surface. Unknown keys (a tour's `states` and `dynamic`) are ignored.

fields.description: Derived from panels: every panel's field names in the order declared, duplicates dropped. A client need not send it

panels.description: Published panel name to the fields and controls that panel offers; empty when omitted

surface.description: Which surface this is, e.g. `console` or `me`. Recorded and echoed back, not yet acted on

version.description: Version of the dictionary format the client writes, so a newer client can be recognised rather than misread

SurfacePanel.description: One panel's published vocabulary in a surface dictionary: the fields the assistant may fill and the controls a tour may press

controls.description: Names of controls the surface can press. Recorded only: the assistant has no verb that presses one

fields.description: Names of the fields on this panel the assistant may offer to fill; empty when omitted

SurfaceResponse.description: The surface recorded, and the fields the assistant will now offer to fill

fields.description: Field names the assistant may now fill

SweepSpec.description: A sweep: a cold materialization an agent keeps filled by running a saved view pass after pass, under a budget, until a pass buys nothing

budgetPerTick.description: Most units of paid work (a producer fetch, or a group of an inline judgement) one pass may buy; null takes the host's default

name.description: The sweep's name within its agent; part of the fill's identity, so starting it twice is one fill

view.description: Name of a saved view of this world that takes no arguments: the query each pass runs

SystemStatus.description: Memory, CPU, the document ingest queue, document conversion, and embedding coverage, read now

conversion.description: Active document converter, docling's state, and conversion failures since start

cpu.description: Process and machine CPU load, and the processors the JVM may use

embeddings.description: Embedding model and its provider, and stored chunks still lacking an embedding

ingest.description: Heap budget for document ingests, what running ingests hold of it, and how many wait

memory.description: JVM heap and container memory, in bytes

TagsRequest.description: Body of `PUT /documents/tags`: the document, and the tags it should carry afterwards.

tags.description: The complete set of tags, replacing what the document carried. Each is trimmed, blanks dropped and duplicates collapsed; an empty list removes every tag

uri.description: The document's uri, as GET /documents lists it

TagsResponse.description: What `PUT /documents/tags` answers: whether the document was found, and the tags it now carries.

status.description: `tagged` when the tags were replaced, `not_found` when the caller's world holds no document at that uri

tags.description: The tags the document now carries, cleaned as stored. Empty when `not_found`

uri.description: The uri the request named, echoed back

TextIngestRequest.description: Body of `POST /documents/text`: inline text saved as a file in the world's `data/documents` directory and ingested from there.

content.description: The text to ingest, written to the file as given

name.description: File name to save the text under in the world's `data/documents` directory, overwriting a file of that name; also the title when the text yields none

tags.description: Tags to put on the document and its chunks. Blanks are dropped and duplicates collapsed; absent means none

ThemeApplied.description: A theme switch that took effect for the current session

status.description: Always "applied": the only outcome this body reports, since an unknown theme answers 404 with no body

theme.description: The name of the theme now active, as the theme list and the stylesheet path spell it

Thread.description: A conversation the caller shares with their agents. GET /threads lists them, POST /threads answers the one it started, and GET /threads/{id} carries it with its messages.

createdAt.description: When the thread was started, as an ISO-8601 instant

id.description: Thread id, a UUIDv7 string; the {id} in /threads/{id}

ownerId.description: User id of the person who owns the thread; always the caller, since only the owner can read it

title.description: Title as given when the thread was started, trimmed; "Untitled" when none was given

updatedAt.description: Last activity in the thread, as an ISO-8601 instant; the list is sorted on it, newest first

ThreadList.description: The caller's threads with their agents; answered by GET /threads

threads.description: The caller's threads, most recently active first

ThreadMessage.description: One message in a thread, with what it attached. POST /threads/{id}/messages answers the one posted; GET /threads/{id} lists them all, oldest first.

attachments.description: Things attached to the message, frozen when it was sent; at most 10

createdAt.description: When the message was written, as an ISO-8601 instant

id.description: Message id, a UUIDv7 string, so ids sort in the order the messages were written

inReplyTo.description: Id of the message this one answers; null on a message that answers none, such as a person's post

mentions.description: Names of the agents this message @mentioned, limited to agents that exist in the world; empty when it addressed none by name

text.description: The words of the message; may be empty on a person's message that only attaches things, and is "(no answer)" when an agent replied with nothing

threadId.description: Id of the thread the message is in

wordsOnly.description: True on an agent's answer to a message that carried no attachment, so it was given from the words alone

ThreadView.description: A thread with all its messages and the agents still answering; answered by GET /threads/{id}

messages.description: Every message in the thread, oldest first

thread.description: The thread's own record: its id, owner, title and timestamps, without its messages

waitingOn.description: Names of the agents still working on an answer, sorted; empty when none is. Not kept across a restart, so an answer in progress then is no longer shown as awaited.

ThreadsResponse.description: The answer of GET /email/threads: recent threads from every connected account, or an error and an empty list.

error.description: Why the request failed, a bad parameter or a provider failure; null on success

threads.description: Threads from every connected account with messages in the requested window, at most maxPerAccount per account; empty when error is set

TimeoutsConfig.description: This world's execution-timeout overrides, in seconds; a null field inherits the deployment default. Part of GET /config

kgQuerySeconds.description: Ceiling for one knowledge-graph (Virtual Cypher) query execution, in seconds; null, zero or negative inherits assistant.lens.kg-query-timeout

scriptSeconds.description: Ceiling for one code-mode sandbox script run, in seconds; null, zero or negative inherits assistant.code-mode.script-timeout

TimerSummary.description: One outcome of a timed meter, combined across every realm, function and host series that carries it

count.description: Number of recordings with this outcome since the process started

maxMillis.description: Longest single duration in milliseconds, as Micrometer's decaying max: recent recordings only, not since start, and 0 after a quiet spell

outcome.description: Value of the meter's outcome tag, e.g. ok, guest_error or timeout for a dispatch; built, cache_hit or failed for a build

totalMillis.description: Sum of their durations since the process started, in milliseconds

TipSchedule.description: When a tip is posted to the acting user's inbox, as a frequency preset and an hour; the body of PUT /hints/schedule

frequency.description: How often a tip is posted; NEVER turns tips off. Defaults to WEEKDAYS when absent

hour.description: Hour of day, 0-23, in the user's own time zone. Defaults to 9 when absent; outside 0-23 is a 400

TipScheduleView.description: The acting user's tip schedule and the cron expression it runs on; answered by GET and PUT /hints/schedule

cron.description: Spring six-field cron expression the schedule runs on (second minute hour day month day-of-week), read in the user's own time zone; null when frequency is NEVER

frequency.description: How often a tip is posted to the inbox; NEVER means tips are off

hour.description: Hour of day (0-23) the tip is posted, in the user's own time zone

TourDeletedResponse.description: Whether a saved tour was removed

deleted.description: True when a tour this user saved was removed. False when the tour is not the caller's to remove — a realm's or the world's own — or no deletable tour has that id

yaml.description: The tour's YAML, as exported or as a realm would ship it

TourListResponse.description: Every tour declared for a world

tours.description: The tours, shipped, realm-contributed and user-saved alike; on import, only the tours just stored
