TourRefusal.description: Why a tour was refused, in the server's own words

error.description: The refusal, as a sentence to show the user

TourStepStatusRequest.description: The parameters a tour has collected so far, bound into the step's precondition

params.description: Values the tour has collected so far, by name, bound as query parameters of the step's precondition

TourStepStatusResponse.description: Whether a step's precondition is already satisfied

detail.description: Why, when the status is UNKNOWN — the query error in the author's words

status.description: DONE when the step's precondition returned a row, or when its `when` condition returned none (the step does not apply here); TODO when it is not yet satisfied or has no precondition; UNKNOWN when its query could not be run or the tour or step does not exist, in which case the client should run the step anyway

TourStepView.description: One step, as its file declared it — minus the precondition, which stays server-side

presentation.description: Everything the step's YAML declared except its `doneWhen` and `when` preconditions, carried through uninterpreted — the client owns that vocabulary

watchable.description: This step HAS a precondition, without saying what it is. A client that hands a step to the user can then poll for it and carry on by itself when the world says the user has done the thing — go and connect a coding agent, and the tour notices. Without this flag a client would have to poll every hand-over blindly, spending a query every few seconds on steps that can never come true.

TourSummary.description: A tour: its identity, its provenance, and the client's own declarations

declaredId.description: What the tour's own file called it — the id that survives an export

deletable.description: This world can remove it. NOT the same as userSaved: a tour hand-written into a user's own config is theirs but is not this server's to delete, so a client offering Delete for it would offer a button that silently does nothing.

id.description: Unique within this world, and what every other call addresses

presentation.description: Everything the tour's YAML declared beyond id and steps, uninterpreted

source.description: The realm that shipped it, or absent for a world's own and a user's own. Carried rather than derived from the id — a namespace prefix is not something a client can reliably strip.

steps.description: The tour's steps in walking order; a step's position here is the `index` the status call takes

userSaved.description: Imported or recorded by this user, rather than shipped by a realm or the world

TransitionRule.description: A named domain transition: matched when one field of an updated item changes in the stated way. Every condition given must hold, and at least one must be given

crossesAbove.description: Matches a numeric field going from at or below this value to above it

crossesBelow.description: Matches a numeric field going from at or above this value to below it

field.description: The dotted path of the field watched. Must be in `compareFields`, or one of an entity's own source, id, name, description or labels

from.description: The JSON value the field must have changed from. Absent matches any

name.description: What to call the transition; reported as the `kind` of each one detected

to.description: The JSON value the field must have changed to. Absent matches any

Upcoming.description: What an agent will do next: its scheduled firings, the routines that wait for a signal, the requests its last duty checks say to expect, work in flight, and its recent counts. Answered by GET /agents/{name}/upcoming and after a skip or run-now

agent.description: Name of the agent, as asked

counts.description: What it has done lately, in the units a budget is set in

expected.description: Duties whose next check is expected to raise requests again

firings.description: Its scheduled duty checks and routines, soonest first, those with no next time last. Only jobs the scheduler holds: a duty whose agent is off duty has none

inFlight.description: Its runs still in progress, from its 500 most recent

onSignals.description: Names of the routines it holds that have no scheduled job: the ones that run when something happens rather than at a time

UpcomingResponse.description: What an agent will do next after a skip or a run-now, or why the change was refused

refused.description: Why the change was refused, in words; null when it was made

upcoming.description: The agent's upcoming work after the change; null when it was refused

UpdateActionRequest.description: The body of POST /actions/spec/{name}: changes to a prompted action saved in the world's config/actions directory. A field left out or null keeps its current value.

description.description: Replacement description of what the action does

inputTypeNames.description: Input type names replacing the whole current set

llmModel.description: Replacement model name the action runs on

llmTemperature.description: Replacement sampling temperature the action runs at

prompt.description: Replacement Jinja2 prompt template the action runs

references.description: Skill, reference-document or memory names replacing the whole current list

tools.description: Tool names replacing the whole current list

UpdatePersonalityRequest.description: Body of PUT /world/personalities/{slug}/files: personality files to save, kept only if the persona still renders

files.description: File name to its full new content. Names are among `identity.yml`, `personality.jinja`, `behaviours.jinja`, `guardrails.jinja`, `response_format.jinja` and `verbosity.jinja`; any other is refused. Files not named are left as they are

UpdateRequest.description: The operator's architectural principles for PUT /admin/principles, replacing the shipped default for the whole appliance

content.description: The principles as plain text or markdown, stored as written and handed to coding agents verbatim in their authoring brief. Must not be blank; DELETE /admin/principles returns to the shipped default

UpdateWatchRequest.description: The body of PATCH /watches/{watchId}; a field left out or null keeps that setting as it is.

clearCron.description: True removes the schedule, so the watch runs only on request; ignored when cron is also given

clearDelivery.description: True removes delivery, so diffs are kept in history only; ignored when delivery is also given

cron.description: Replacement cron expression, in the form create takes; blank removes the schedule. Null keeps the current schedule unless clearCron is true

delivery.description: Delivery replacing the whole current one; a masked secret or header value sent back keeps the stored value. Null keeps the current delivery unless clearDelivery is true

diffSpec.description: Comparison policy replacing the whole current one; null keeps it

enabled.description: True switches the watch on, false switches it off; null leaves it as it is

firstRunPolicy.description: Replacement first-run policy; null keeps the current one

name.description: New label; null or blank keeps the current one

params.description: Lens arguments replacing the whole current map; null keeps the current ones

UrlIngestRequest.description: Body of `POST /documents/url` and `POST /documents/ingests/url`: a page or file to fetch and ingest into the caller's world.

fromOrgDomain.description: Domain of the organisation the document is really from, recorded as its publisher. Absent or blank means the URL's host

tags.description: Tags to put on the document and its chunks. Blanks are dropped and duplicates collapsed; absent means none

url.description: The URL to fetch — a web page, PDF or other document. It also becomes the document's uri

UserContextView.description: The user's active memory context and the contexts they can switch to, answered by GET /context and PUT /context/current

contexts.description: Context names this user has documents under, with the active one first when it has none yet. A context that holds only memories is not listed

current.description: Name of the active context, which new documents and memories belong to. `personal` until the user switches

VerbSpec.description: One verb the user's machine offers, as the sensor declares it to POST /sensor/capabilities

args.description: Each argument's name mapped to what it means. Empty for a verb that takes none

description.description: What the verb does, in words shown to the assistant's model

group.description: The consent group the verb belongs to, as the sensor names it (the Me app uses `see` and `act`). The appliance does not interpret it

name.description: Verb name, carried as a command's `kind` when the verb is asked for, e.g. `tabs.find`

Verification.description: Whether the signed-in user's receipt chain still says what it said when written, and where it first breaks; answered by GET /receipts/verify. It shows an edit, not that the record is complete

brokenAt.description: The seq of the first receipt that breaks the chain; null when intact

intact.description: True when every receipt follows the one before it and hashes to what it says

receipts.description: How many receipts the owner's chain holds

why.description: Why the chain breaks there: the receipt does not follow the one before it, or it was changed after it was written. Null when intact

ViewDebugInfo.description: A saved view visible to the acting user — world or realm tier — with its definition and, for a materialised view, its cache state. The items of `GET /views`.

cachedMembers.description: Nodes — or, for a row snapshot, rows — the cache holds. Null for a regular view, or a materialised one with nothing cached.

cypher.description: The view's Cypher body, trimmed, with any `$name` parameter references as declared.

dataContract.description: The ODCS contract the view is pinned to, and in which mode. Absent when it is not contracted.

description.description: One line on what the view answers. Empty when it declares none.

expiresAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the cache expires; may already be past. Null for a regular view, or a materialised one with nothing cached.

materialized.description: True when reads are served from a cache that is recomputed once `ttl` lapses.

name.description: The view's name, which a query uses as a label and `/views/{name}` paths take.

outputLabel.description: The node label the view's rows are. Null for a tabular view, and for a materialised view that keeps its rows as a snapshot.

params.description: Declared bind variables by name. Empty for an unparameterized view, and always for a materialised one.

source.description: The realm that shipped the view. Null for a view of the world's own.

ttl.description: Cache lifetime, e.g. `30m`, `2h`, `1d`. Null for a regular view.

ViewParamSpec.description: A declared bind variable of a saved view, referenced as $name in its Cypher and supplied per invocation, keyed by that name wherever a view's params are declared or listed

choices.description: The fixed set of values this param accepts — rendered as a select, enforced at invocation. Absent = any value of the declared type.

default.description: Used when an invocation omits this param. Absent = required on invocation, unless required: false.

description.description: What the argument means — rendered verbatim as the field's hint.

required.description: false lets an invocation omit a param that has no default; it is then bound to null.

type.description: The coercion applied to supplied values, and the form control a UI renders (int/number a number field, boolean a checkbox, date a date picker). float and double are aliases of number.

VoiceOptionView.description: One voice the user can choose for spoken replies

id.description: Voice id to send as voiceName, e.g. `aura-2-phoebe-en`

label.description: Name to show for the voice

VoiceProfileView.description: The user's voice preferences and the voices on offer, answered by GET and PUT /profile/voice

available.description: False when no voice can be offered to this user (no voice key, or the voice catalogue is empty or could not be read); a client should then hide voice controls

effects.description: Effect presets this deployment offers, e.g. `warm`, `radio`, `echo`

selectedEffects.description: Effect presets applied to this user's spoken replies; empty for none

voiceName.description: The chosen voice id, or null for the deployment's default voice

voices.description: Voices this user can choose from; empty when not available

VoiceSessionView.description: The credential a browser opens its Deepgram audio socket with and the settings that go with it, answered by GET /voice/session

effects.description: Audio effect presets the user chose for spoken replies, such as warm, radio or echo. Empty for none

replacements.description: Transcription corrections, each written heard:intended, to pass to Deepgram so it hears this world's vocabulary

speed.description: Speaking rate as a multiplier of Deepgram's natural pace, where 1.0 is natural

token.description: The Deepgram credential for this session: the user's own key if their world stores one, else this installation's or deployment's. Ask again for each socket rather than caching it

transcriber.description: Deepgram speech-recognition engine to transcribe with, such as nova-3

voice.description: Deepgram voice that speaks replies, such as aura-2-phoebe-en: the user's chosen voice, else the deployment's default

VoiceUpdateBody.description: Voice preferences to store, the body of PUT /profile/voice. Both fields are replaced

effects.description: Effect presets to apply; blank entries are dropped, and an empty or absent list clears them

voiceName.description: Voice id from the voices list; absent or blank resets to the deployment's default voice

WebFetchConfig.description: This world's choice of strategies for the built-in fetch and crawl tools; null fields inherit the server defaults. Part of GET /config

crawler.description: Site-crawl strategy for crawl; bounded is the only one, so any other name falls back to it. Null or blank inherits the server default

retriever.description: Page retriever for fetch: tika (in-process fetch and extraction) or reader-service (only when the server configures one); null or blank inherits the server default, and an unknown name falls back to tika

count.description: How many events the body carried

errors.description: How many threw. A partial failure still answers 200 or 202, so a caller must read this rather than the status code

processed.description: How many were dispatched and ran

queued.description: How many were queued against an unconfigured source

WebhookBatch.description: A batch of events, counted by outcome. Answers 200 when any ran, 202 when any queued, and 500 only when EVERY event failed

WebhookConfiguredSource.description: A webhook source this world can handle

action.description: The action that handles it, prefix included

description.description: The action's own description, where it declares one

source.description: The source name a provider posts to, with the `webhook-` prefix removed

output.description: Whatever the handler returned, verbatim and unshaped — a handler's output is the handler's business

WebhookProcessed.description: A single event was dispatched to its handler and ran

message.description: Why it was queued rather than handled, written to be shown

source.description: The source the event was queued against

WebhookQueued.description: A single event was accepted but not dispatched, because its source is not configured yet

WebhookQueuedSource.description: A source with events waiting for a handler

source.description: The source the events arrived for

WebhookReceipt.description: What the webhook endpoint answers: a receipt for the event, a refusal, or a provider's registration handshake

message.description: What went wrong, written to be shown

WebhookRefused.description: The request was refused: 400 for a body that would not parse, 500 for a dispatch that threw

WebhookStatus.description: Where this appliance receives webhooks, and what it is configured to receive

configured.description: The webhook sources this world declares handlers for

localUrl.description: The address reachable on this machine

publicUrl.description: The internet-reachable address, when a Tailscale funnel was detected. Null means providers outside this machine cannot reach it

queued.description: Sources holding events that arrived before a handler existed, with how many are waiting

tailscale.description: What the Tailscale probe found. Open by contract — it mirrors whatever `tailscale status` reported

webhookUrl.description: The template a provider should be pointed at, with {source} left to substitute. Uses the public URL when one was detected, otherwise the local one

reason.description: Which check refused it. Deliberately coarse — a precise reason would tell an attacker which half of the credential was wrong

WebhookUnauthorized.description: The caller was not admitted: signature verification, tenant resolution or source installation failed

encryptedToken.description: The hex HMAC-SHA256 of plainToken, keyed by the provider's stored webhook secret

plainToken.description: The token the provider sent, echoed back unchanged

WebhookUrlValidation.description: A provider's URL-registration handshake. THIS SHAPE IS THE PROVIDER'S, not this API's: Zoom requires exactly these two fields and no status, so it must not be made to resemble the other receipts.

WorldChanged.description: A world was created or switched to. The same three keys either way; `status` says which happened

name.description: The world's name

path.description: Where the world lives on the appliance's disk

status.description: `created` from a create, `switched` from a switch

WorldConfig.description: The user's world configuration as loaded from the world's config/world.yml, over the deployment defaults. Answered by GET /config; its parts are edited through the narrower /config endpoints

actionCompilerLlm.description: Stored setting for action compilation, chat_best role by default; nothing reads it at runtime

activePersonality.description: Slug of the active personality, a directory under behaviour/personalities/; adaptive by default

apiExplorerLlm.description: Stored setting for API exploration, chat_best role by default; nothing reads it at runtime

chat.description: Model the user chats with, by role or pinned model; null inherits the deployment chat model

codingLlm.description: Model the app builder (vibe coder) writes code with; null inherits the deployment vibe-coder model

collectorConfig.description: Memory-dedup sweep overrides; null inherits every deployment default

fallbackCodingLlm.description: Model the app builder uses for the one call after a failed build with codingLlm, typically a stronger one; null inherits the deployment fallback, if any

filesTrustedRoots.description: Absolute directories the files producer may follow symlinks into from the world's data/ sandbox; relative or nonexistent entries are ignored. Empty by default: nothing outside the sandbox is readable

lensLlm.description: Model that turns a natural-language question into Cypher (kg-ask); null inherits assistant.lens.llm

llmRoles.description: This world's LLM role overrides, keyed by role id (e.g. code_best, chat_best): the model and reasoning effort every call naming that role resolves to here. An absent role inherits the deployment's embabel.models.llms; empty by default

mcpMode.description: What a connected coding agent is here to do: ASSISTANT (use the world) or DEVELOPER (also install and author realms); null means ASSISTANT

memoryLlm.description: Stored setting for memory extraction, chat_cheap role by default; nothing reads it at runtime

notificationRouting.description: The user's notification routing; null inherits the deployment defaults for every tier and for quiet hours

plannerLlm.description: Model the typed planner uses to decompose a /plan request into an action graph; null follows the chat model

rankerLlm.description: Model the chat ranker uses to extract typed inputs from a message; null inherits assistant.ranker.llm

sandboxDockerimage.description: Docker image for this world's code-mode sandbox; null uses the appliance's sandbox image (ghcr.io/embabel/assistant-sandbox:latest unless the operator set assistant.sandbox-image)

timeouts.description: Execution-timeout overrides; null inherits every deployment default

toolRouterLlm.description: Stored setting for tool routing, chat_cheap role by default; nothing reads it at runtime

version.description: World format version the file was last written at; currently 2. Older versions are migrated at load

webFetch.description: Fetch and crawl tool strategies; null inherits the server defaults

WorldDeleted.description: A world was deleted, with everything in it. Carries no path, because there is no longer one

name.description: The world that was deleted

WorldDocumentContent.description: A world document's content, capped at the first 10000 characters

content.description: The document's text, truncated to 10000 characters

name.description: The document name that was asked for, echoed back

size.description: The file's full size in bytes, before truncation

WorldDocumentMissing.description: A document this world does not have. Carries the name asked for rather than a sentence, because the only fact is which name missed

name.description: The document name that was asked for, echoed back unchanged

status.description: Always `not_found` — not the `error` the rest of this surface answers

WorldDocumentSummary.description: One world document, and who last changed it

lastModifiedBy.description: Who or what last wrote it

name.description: The document's name

WorldListing.description: Every world this user has, and which one they are in

current.description: The world the user is currently in, by name

worlds.description: Every world discovered on disk for this user, sorted by name

WorldLlmSettings.description: The model settings of every purpose a world configures, one entry per purpose

chat.description: The model a person talks to

codingLlm.description: The model code is written with

fallbackCodingLlm.description: The model code is written with when the coding model fails

memoryLlm.description: The model memory work runs on

WorldManagementRefusal.description: A refusal from the world management surface. Carries only the reason, with no status word — the status code is the only other fact and the body does not repeat it

error.description: Why the operation was refused, written to be shown. Names the world where the refusal is about a particular one

WorldMcpServerSummary.description: One MCP server a world configures, and how many tools it offers

description.description: What the server is for; empty when it declares nothing

name.description: The server's name

WorldNamedEntry.description: One named thing in a world — a skill, an API, an action or a tool — and what it is for

description.description: What it is for, as it describes itself. Empty, not null, for a tool with no description

name.description: Its name, unique within its list

WorldOverview.description: A summary of everything a world has loaded

mcpServers.description: The MCP servers the world itself configures

path.description: The world's directory on the server

WorldProvisioningStatus.description: How far a world being made for the first time has got. Only `provisioning` is present when nothing is being made

elapsedSeconds.description: Whole seconds since the build started. Absent when nothing is being provisioned

phase.description: The current build phase, lower case. Absent when nothing is being provisioned

provisioning.description: True while this user's world is being built for the first time

saying.description: A sentence describing the phase, written to be shown. Absent when nothing is being provisioned

WorldRealmSummary.description: One installed realm, as its realm.yml describes it

author.description: Who wrote it; empty when it declares nobody

description.description: What the realm does; empty when it declares nothing

name.description: The realm's name

tags.description: The realm's listing tags

url.description: Where the realm lives, or null when its listing names nowhere

WorldRefusal.description: A refusal from the world administration surface: what went wrong, and the word `error` so a client reading the body need not consult the status code

message.description: What was refused and why, written to be shown. Names the offending value where there is one — the unknown mode, the out-of-range threshold, the invalid cron expression

WorldReset.description: A world's config was reset to the template. Its `data/` was left alone, which the warning says out loud

name.description: The world that was reset

warning.description: That the config went back to defaults and the data directory was preserved — said in the body because a caller who reads only the status code would not know the difference between this and a delete

WorldSummary.description: One of a user's worlds, as the listing describes it

active.description: Whether this is the world the user is currently in

name.description: The world's name, which is what the other endpoints take in the path

path.description: Where the world lives on the appliance's disk

WorldToolCatalog.description: Every tool the model can call in this world, by category

WorldTypeSummary.description: One of a world's own types, with the names of its properties

description.description: What the type represents

name.description: The type's name

properties.description: The names of its properties, inherited ones included

WorldWebhookSummary.description: One webhook a world registers: what it listens to and what it runs

action.description: The action a delivery runs; empty when none is named

description.description: What it is for; empty when it declares nothing

events.description: The event names it accepts; empty for all

hasAutoRegister.description: True when the webhook registers itself with its source

name.description: The webhook's name

source.description: The system that sends it

apiKeyAuth.description: An API key minted in the console under Settings → API keys. Also accepted as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

basicAuth.description: The appliance's own user accounts. The Worlds console proxies these on the same origin.

post.description: Compiles a natural language description into a PromptedActionSpec. Uses the AI to generate a Jinja2 prompt template and saves to the world's config/actions directory. The output type defaults to BackgroundMessage when not specified.

requestBody.description: What to compile into a world action. `name` names the action and its file, `config/actions/<name>.yml`, which is overwritten if it exists; `description` is the natural-language brief an LLM turns into the Jinja2 prompt. `inputTypeNames`, `toolNames` and `referenceNames` default to empty, `outputTypeName` to `com.embabel.agent.spec.model.BackgroundMessage`; `llmModel` (default: the platform default) and `llmTemperature` (default `0.0`) are saved on the action and also drive the compiling call, which uses `0.1` when the temperature is not positive

parameters.description: File name of a document directly inside the world's `data/documents` directory, as listed by GET /world/documents; a name that is missing, is a directory, or resolves anywhere else (a subdirectory, `..`) answers 404
parameters.name: name

404.description: Document not found

get.description: Returns MCP servers reachable from this world: those the world itself configured, plus any wired in at the installation level, each with its tool count and tool names.

delete.description: Removes an MCP server entry from the world.

parameters.description: Exact name of an MCP server entry in the world's `config/mcp` files, as shown by GET /world/mcp; servers wired in at the installation level are not world entries and cannot be removed here. Answers 200 whether or not an entry matched
parameters.name: name

get.description: Returns all personalities in the world with slug, display name, source, and active status.

post.description: Creates a world-tier personality — blank, or duplicated from an existing one via `from`. Validated by rendering before it counts; a persona that cannot render is not created.

requestBody.description: The world-tier personality to create: `slug` (trimmed; 1-40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not starting with a hyphen), `name` (the display name written into its `identity.yml`, which is stamped `source: user`) and optional `from` (slug of a personality of any tier whose files are copied; omit for empty sections). Answers 400 when the slug is taken or invalid, `from` is unknown, or the result does not render

400.description: Refused — slug taken, unknown `from`, or the persona does not render

post.summary: Create a personality

delete.description: The active personality is refused — switch first. Realm personalities are removed by uninstalling their realm.

parameters.description: Slug of a world-tier personality the user made; the active personality (switch first), shipped and realm personalities, and unknown slugs answer 400
parameters.name: slug

400.description: Refused — active, realm-owned, or unknown

get.description: The identity and jinja sections of one personality, with whether it is editable. Realm personalities are readable but read-only — duplicating one into the world is how it becomes editable.

parameters.description: Slug of the personality to read, as listed by GET /world/personalities; any tier can be read. An unknown slug answers 404
parameters.name: slug

404.description: Unknown personality

put.description: Sets the active personality for the current world.

parameters.description: Slug of the personality to make active, as listed by GET /world/personalities (any tier: world, shipped or realm); saved as the world's `activePersonality`. An unknown slug answers 400 with the available slugs
parameters.name: slug

400.description: Unknown personality; the response lists the available slugs

put.summary: Switch active personality

put.description: World-tier personalities only; a realm personality answers with the duplicate-first instruction. The save is validated by rendering, and rolls back if the persona no longer renders.

parameters.description: Slug of a world-tier personality the user made; shipped and realm personalities are read-only and answer 400 asking for a duplicate first, as does an unknown slug
parameters.name: slug

requestBody.description: Files to write, keyed by file name (`identity.yml`, `personality.jinja`, `behaviours.jinja`, `guardrails.jinja`, `response_format.jinja`, `verbosity.jinja`), each replacing that file's whole content; files not named are left as they are, and any other name answers 400. If the persona no longer renders afterwards the personality is rolled back to its previous files and the render error returned as 400

400.description: Refused — read-only, unknown files, or the persona does not render

put.summary: Save a personality's files

get.description: What a world being made for the first time is up to. Empty once there is nothing in progress.

200.description: The current phase, or an empty object

get.description: Returns all loaded skills with their descriptions.

post.description: Creates a new local skill with a SKILL.md following the Agent Skills Specification.

requestBody.description: The skill to write to `config/skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md`: `name` (1-64 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen; it becomes the directory name), `description` (at most 1024 characters, written into the frontmatter) and `instructions` (the markdown body). The world is refreshed on success; an existing skill of that name answers 409, an invalid name or over-long description 400

400.description: Invalid input

409.description: Skill already exists

post.summary: Create a local skill

post.description: Clears the local GitHub skills disk cache and rebuilds the world so skills are re-fetched on next load.

200.description: Skills cache cleared and world rebuilt

post.summary: Refresh GitHub skills

delete.description: Removes a skill entry from the world.

parameters.description: Text matched against the `url` and `path` of the skill entries in the world's `config/skills` manifests; every entry containing it (a substring match, not an exact name) is removed and the world rebuilt. Skills created with POST /world/skills live under `config/skills/local` and are not manifest entries, so this does not remove them. Answers 200 whether or not anything matched
parameters.name: name

get.description: Returns all tools grouped by category (skills, apiTools, mcpTools, documentTools, progressTools, statusTools).
get.summary: List all tools available to the LLM

get.description: Returns all dynamic type definitions in the world.
Lists all worlds for the current user.

post.description: Creates a new world from the default template. The JSON body requires a name key; the name must not contain slashes or dots-dots.

requestBody.description: `name` (required): the new world's directory name among the current user's worlds, trimmed; missing, blank, or containing `/` or `..`, it answers 400, and a name that already holds a world answers 409. The world is cloned from the deployment's bootstrap template; creating it does not switch to it

400.description: Missing or invalid name

409.description: World already exists

post.summary: Create world

delete.description: Deletes a world. Cannot delete the currently active world.

parameters.description: Name of one of the current user's worlds, as listed by GET /worlds; its whole directory, `data/` included, is deleted. The active world answers 400 (switch first), a name with no directory 404
parameters.name: name

400.description: Cannot delete active world

404.description: World not found

post.description: Wipes the world's `config/` directory and re-clones it from the default template. **The `data/` directory is left untouched** — documents, vibe-coded apps, tasks, learnings, generated artifacts and entered secrets are preserved. To wipe everything including data, delete the world instead.

parameters.description: Name of one of the current user's worlds, as listed by GET /worlds; its `config/` is replaced from the bootstrap template and `data/` kept. The active world is rebuilt straight away; a name with no directory answers 404
parameters.name: name

200.description: World config reset to defaults; data preserved

404.description: World not found

post.summary: Factory reset world

post.description: Switches the current user to a different world.

parameters.description: Name of one of the current user's worlds, as listed by GET /worlds; a name with no world content answers 404. The choice is saved on the user, so it holds across sessions
parameters.name: name

404.description: World not found

post.summary: Switch world
